company_assessment.market_position: Videa (legal entity Videa Health, Inc., founded 2018 out of MIT by Florian Hillen, headquartered in Boston, MA) is the most adopted dental AI platform in North America, used by 90,000+ clinicians across 60+ leading Dental Support Organizations (DSOs) including 8 of North America's 10 largest DSOs and 80%+ of the top 10 dental networks. The company rebranded from VideaHealth to Videa in April 2026 when it expanded go-to-market beyond enterprise DSOs to independent private dental practices. It has raised $60M+ across Series A and Series B rounds led by Spark Capital and Threshold Ventures, respectively.

strengths.details: Videa has evolved from a single-feature X-ray detector to a unified platform spanning Clinical Assist, Voice Notes, Voice Perio, Daily Dashboard, Insights, Clean Claims, AutoVerify, ClaimsAI, and the new Ambient Intelligence category. Each new module layers onto the same FDA-cleared engine and embedded Dentrix deployment, turning each practice into a multi-product account and materially expanding ARR per site over time.
strengths.headline: Platform expansion from diagnostics to full revenue cycle unlocks massive wallet share.

strengths.details: With 500M+ X-rays analyzed annually and ~90,000 clinicians feeding real-world feedback, Videa's training corpus and benchmarking insights (e.g., Insights product) widen every quarter — a flywheel that is structurally hard for late entrants to replicate and should drive widening accuracy advantages and stickier renewals.
strengths.headline: Data-network effects compound with every X-ray analyzed at scale.

strengths.details: One-click activation inside Dentrix and Dentrix Ascend positions Videa as the default AI layer across the largest PMS installed base. As the April 2026 rebrand opens the independent-practice segment, this embedment should drive low-CAC land-and-expand into tens of thousands of additional practices without a proportionate salesforce expansion.
strengths.headline: Embedded Henry Schein One partnership unlocks the long tail of independent practices.

strengths.details: Clean Claims and AutoVerify target claim denials (50% reduction in early results) and eligibility verification (95%+ payer coverage), addressing roughly $15B in dental RCM waste per company commentary. Scaling these modules converts Videa from a clinical-AI vendor into a margin-recovery platform, materially expanding the revenue envelope per customer.
strengths.headline: AI-led revenue cycle management attacks a large, under-digitized dental RCM market.

strengths.details: North American DSOs are rapidly consolidating, and Videa already covers 8 of the 10 largest networks. As those customers grow via M&A and as Tier-2/3 DSOs professionalize, Videa's proven multi-week enterprise rollout playbook (Aspen 6 weeks, Heartland 10 weeks, Great Expressions 2 weeks) should translate into faster, larger enterprise wins with limited incremental go-to-market cost.
strengths.headline: DSO consolidation tailwind accelerates both land and expand.

weakness.details: With Aspen and Heartland alone representing ~2,600+ practices of Videa's footprint, any multi-year renewal reset, in-house AI build, or partial rollout contraction at these accounts would compress revenue and operating leverage in lockstep — a vulnerability that grows as the company adds fewer, larger customers before broader diversification.
weakness.headline: Mega-DSO renewals concentrate revenue risk at scale.

weakness.details: Videa's 35 FDA-cleared detections are described as more than double any competitor, but competitors such as Pearl and Overjet are steadily accumulating clearances of their own. Once a rival approaches parity on detection breadth and accuracy, pricing power, win rates, and renewal economics will all come under pressure.
weakness.headline: Competitor parity on FDA clearances could erode the '2x' moat.

weakness.details: The April 2026 pivot to independent practices requires a fundamentally different sales motion (low-touch, demo-driven, likely smaller average contract values) than the existing DSO field-sales engine. If SMB conversion lags or churn rises, customer acquisition costs could balloon before unit economics mature, compressing margins even as headline clinician count grows.
weakness.headline: Independent-practice expansion could dilute margins on an unproven SMB motion.

weakness.details: Embedded Dentrix and Dentrix Ascend integrations are core to Videa's go-to-market; a strategic dispute, exclusivity shift to a rival AI vendor, or material change in Henry Schein One's AI roadmap could simultaneously affect activation, upsell, and competitive positioning across a large portion of Videa's installed base.
weakness.headline: Henry Schein One channel concentration is a single point of failure.

weakness.details: As Videa pushes into higher-risk categories — Ambient Intelligence, AI-driven revenue cycle decisions, OrthoAI/ImplantAI — it will face more demanding FDA, payer, and clinical-oversight scrutiny. Any forced re-clearance, post-market surveillance event, or new AI-specific rules could delay launches and raise compliance costs at exactly the moment the company is scaling into new modules.
weakness.headline: Increasing AI and SaMD regulatory scrutiny could slow product velocity.

competitive_moat.details: Videa's AI analyzes 500M+ dental X-rays annually, creating an unparalleled proprietary training dataset that compounds with scale and is not replicable by new entrants. This data flywheel underpins the 35 FDA-cleared detections — more than double any other dental AI vendor.

Embedded inside Henry Schein One's Dentrix and Dentrix Ascend platforms, plus integrations with OpenDental, Patterson, Planet DDS, SOTA Dental, ClearDent, and Dentsply Sirona, Videa reaches the installed base of major practice management systems. 8 of North America's 10 largest DSOs and 60+ leading DSOs are deployed, representing 80%+ of the top 10 dental networks.

35 FDA-cleared detections for dental conditions (caries, calculus, periapical radiolucency, and others) constitute a regulatory moat requiring clinical validation that competitors must replicate, doubling the next-best vendor's count.

Deep integration with practice management systems (Dentrix, OpenDental, Patterson, Trinity), workflow embedding at chairside and front desk, and clinician training on AI-assisted diagnostics create meaningful friction — sustained 95% usage rate evidences stickiness.

90,000+ active clinicians generate continuous usage data and clinical feedback that improve detection accuracy and template coverage (e.g., 35+ Voice Notes procedure templates), producing a learning flywheel that benefits existing and new customers.

MIT-originated brand pedigree, clinical leadership via the AI Leadership Council with CMOs/CSOs of major DSOs (Aspen, Heartland, 42 North, Gen4), and a 2025 Inc. 5000 rank of #28 (highest of any dental organization in any category) reinforce category leadership.

key_risks.details: Just two customers (Aspen Dental at 1,100+ practices and Heartland Dental at 1,500+ practices) account for a very large share of deployed endpoints. Loss or downsizing of either account would materially impact revenue and operating leverage.
key_risks.headline: Heavy customer concentration in a few mega-DSOs creates renewal and churn concentration risk.

key_risks.details: Companies such as Pearl and Overjet are pursuing the same dental imaging AI category with similar FDA-clearance roadmaps; differentiation must be defended continuously, and competitor parity on detection count could erode the current '2x' advantage over time.
key_risks.headline: Crowded competitive landscape in dental AI from well-funded rivals.

key_risks.details: Significant go-to-market leverage flows through Dentrix/Dentrix Ascend; a Henry Schein One strategy shift, pricing dispute, or competing AI partnership could compress Videa's activation funnel and embedment in core PMS workflows.
key_risks.headline: Distribution dependency on Henry Schein One's Dentrix ecosystem is a structural channel risk.

key_risks.details: The April 2026 rebrand explicitly expanded Videa from large DSOs to independent private practices, moving from field-sales to high-velocity SMB sales without historical traction data — execution risk on unit economics and CAC in a fragmented long-tail market.
key_risks.headline: New SMB / independent-practice GTM is unproven after a long enterprise-only focus.

key_risks.details: Operating at 51–100 employees while serving 90,000+ clinicians, 1,500+ practices at the largest customer, and multiple regulated SaaS products elevates concentration risk on founder/CEO Florian Hillen and limits resilience if key clinical or regulatory staff depart.
key_risks.headline: Key-person and founder dependency with very lean headcount for the operational footprint.

key_risks.details: Sales depend on continuing to hold FDA clearances across an expanding set of detections; any future adverse event report, recall, or tightening of FDA's SaMD/AI/ML oversight framework could disrupt launches such as Ambient Intelligence and upcoming AI capabilities.
key_risks.headline: Regulatory and clinical-liability exposure from being an FDA-regulated SaMD.

key_highlights.details: Videa is used by 90,000+ active clinicians at 60+ leading DSOs and processes 500M+ X-rays annually. This scale provides both a defensible training-data advantage and embedded workflow presence.
key_highlights.headline: Massive clinical user base of 90,000+ active clinicians across 60+ DSOs creates a strong data and distribution moat.

key_highlights.details: Videa's Clinical Assist has 35 FDA-cleared dental condition detections (caries, calculus, periapical radiolucency, etc.), explicitly described as more than double any other AI vendor in dentistry. This regulatory barrier is hard for competitors to match quickly.
key_highlights.headline: Regulatory moat: 35 FDA-cleared AI detections, more than double any competing dental AI vendor.

key_highlights.details: Including deployments at Aspen Dental (1,100+ practices), Heartland Dental (1,500+ practices), and Great Expressions (210+ practices). 80%+ of the 10 largest North American dental networks are on Videa — exceptional distribution depth.
key_highlights.headline: Deep enterprise entrenchment: 8 of North America's 10 largest DSOs run on Videa.

key_highlights.details: Customers report 46% more cavities detected, 10% drop in diagnostic errors, 20% higher case acceptance, 50% reduction in claim denials, and $78,268 average additional annual revenue per practice with 95% sustained usage — compelling payback that supports expansion and renewals.
key_highlights.headline: Quantified, strong customer ROI drives high sustained usage and case-acceptance lift.

launches.title: CareStack and Alphaeon Patient Financing Announce New Integration to Help Practices Increase Case Acceptance, Improve Patient Access, and Accelerate Growth
launches.ai_summary: CareStack and Alphaeon Patient Financing announced a new integration that embeds patient financing options directly within CareStack's cloud-based dental practice management platform. The integration aims to address rising patient financial responsibility as a barrier to treatment by enabling practices to present flexible payment options within their existing workflows. This partnership is designed to improve case acceptance rates, reduce administrative burden on staff, and support practice growth by making financing more accessible at the point of care.

launches.full_text:
New integration streamlines patient financing within CareStack’s practice management platform, making it easier for providers to help patients move forward with care. NEWPORT BEACH, Calif., June 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — CareStack, a leading cloud-based dental practice management platform, and Alphaeon Patient Financing, a premier patient financing solution designed for elective healthcare, today announced the launch of a new integration that helps practices seamlessly incorporate patient financing into their existing workflows.



The integration is designed to address one of the most significant challenges facing healthcare providers today: helping patients confidently move forward with treatment in an environment where patient financial responsibility continues to rise. “Financial concerns remain one of the biggest barriers between patients and treatment,” said Abhi Krishna, Chief Executive Officer of CareStack. “By integrating Alphaeon into CareStack, we’re helping practices make accessible financing part of the care journey, enabling more patients to move forward with recommended treatment, while improving case acceptance and practice growth for our customers.” By connecting CareStack’s comprehensive practice management capabilities with Alphaeon’s financing platform, providers can offer patients flexible payment options directly within their workflow, reducing financial friction, improving operational efficiency, and increasing treatment acceptance. “Patients are increasingly seeking flexible ways to pay for care, and providers need tools that make those conversations easier,” said Thomas Ervesun, Chief Executive Officer, Alphaeon. “By integrating Alphaeon directly within CareStack, we’re helping practices remove barriers that often stand between patients and treatment. Together, we’re creating a better experience for providers, staff, and the patients they serve.” Addressing a Growing Industry Challenge As deductibles, out-of-pocket expenses, and elective treatment costs continue to rise, financial concerns have become one of the leading reasons patients delay or decline recommended care. For practices, this often results in: Lower case acceptance rates

Delayed treatment starts

Lost production opportunities

Increased pressure on front-office teams

Slower revenue growth The new CareStack and Alphaeon integration helps practices proactively address these challenges by making financing more accessible, visible, and actionable at the point of care. Key Benefits of the Integration The integration enables practices to: Present financing options within existing workflows

Reduce administrative burden on clinical and front-office teams

Help patients make informed treatment decisions with confidence

Improve treatment conversion and case acceptance rates

Increase revenue opportunities through higher treatment completion

Deliver a more convenient and patient-friendly financial experience Supporting Practice Growth Through Better Financial Experiences The integration reflects a growing trend among leading healthcare organizations: recognizing that patient financing is no longer simply a payment solution, but a strategic growth tool. When patients have access to financing options that fit their needs, providers can help more patients move forward with treatment plans, improve patient satisfaction, and strengthen practice performance. With Alphaeon’s industry-leading provider support, competitive financing offers, and patient-first approach combined with CareStack’s modern cloud-based platform, practices now have a powerful solution to help drive both operational efficiency and practice growth. Availability The CareStack and Alphaeon integration is now available to eligible CareStack customers. To learn more about the integration and upcoming educational opportunities, visit myalphaeoncredit.com/carestack. About CareStack CareStack is a leading cloud-based dental practice management platform designed to simplify operations, improve patient engagement, and help dental organizations scale efficiently. Its all-in-one platform supports scheduling, clinical workflows, billing, analytics, patient communications, and more for practices of all sizes. About Alphaeon Alphaeon is a patient financing solution that helps patients access elective healthcare procedures and treatments through flexible payment options. Trusted by providers nationwide, Alphaeon helps practices improve patient affordability, increase treatment acceptance, and support long-term growth backed by a 24/7 provider-hotline answered in 60 seconds or less. Learn more about our provider solutions at myalphaeoncredit.com. company_assessment.market_position: CareStack, legally Good Methods Global Inc., is a privately held dental software company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Celebration, Florida, with engineering hubs in Trivandrum, Kochi, and Bangalore, and sales operations in London and Sydney. The company serves more than 3,000 dental practices across the United States, the United Kingdom, and Australia, with the most concentrated footprint in multi-location DSOs and emerging dental groups. CareStack has raised over $145 million in cumulative funding from Accel, Delta Dental, Eight Roads Ventures, F-Prime, Steadview Capital, and Straumann, and has acquired Waybeo.

strengths.details: VoiceStack (24/7 AI phone), Aeka (AI imaging), and AI-assisted clinical documentation are natively integrated into the PMS rather than bolted on. As dental labor shortages and wage pressure persist, the value of automating phone triage, documentation, and imaging interpretation should compound — and CareStack is positioned to capture this spend via its growing add-on module attach rate and the Forrester-validated 6-month payback narrative.
strengths.headline: AI-native platform positioned to capture dental workflow automation spend

strengths.details: CareStack's primary customer segment is DSOs and emerging dental groups (3-10 locations), where it offers unified scheduling, consolidated reporting, and centralized operations. With the US DSO market continuing to consolidate and larger enterprise groups seeking to escape fragmented legacy systems (Forrester cited $280K consolidation savings), CareStack's purpose-built DSO architecture should see increased large-deal win rates.
strengths.headline: DSO consolidation tailwind drives demand for unified multi-location PMS

strengths.details: CareStack already has 500+ UK practices (with NHS-specific modules) and 2,000+ Australian dentists, plus localized support and sales presence in both markets. UK private-mix case studies (Dental Excellence UK growing from 40% to 65% private) demonstrate pull. Continued penetration in these and adjacent geographies (e.g., Canada, EU) offers meaningful TAM expansion without proportional R&D spend.
strengths.headline: International expansion provides geographic runway beyond saturated US

strengths.details: Beyond the core PMS subscription, CareStack offers seven integrated Enhanced Growth Solutions (VoiceStack, Aeka, CS Pay, ACE DSN, CareRevenue, VirtualAssistant, CS Membership) plus the AI Suite. As customers mature on the platform, attach of these high-value modules (especially outsourced CareRevenue RCM and CS Membership) expands revenue per practice without new customer acquisition cost.
strengths.headline: Add-on module monetization drives ARPU expansion within existing book

strengths.details: Straumann (parent of Good Methods Global Inc., the CareStack operating entity) is one of the largest dental implant and equipment companies globally. This strategic ownership provides CareStack with distribution channels, customer introductions, and cross-sell opportunities into Straumann's customer base — a relationship that should accelerate enterprise penetration beyond what an independent SaaS could achieve.
strengths.headline: Straumann strategic backing unlocks distribution into dental enterprise ecosystem

weakness.details: Henry Schein One (Dentrix) and Patterson (Eaglesoft) have decades of installed base, deeper reseller networks, and the ability to bundle hardware, supplies, and software. As DSOs seek vendor consolidation, these incumbents may offer aggressively priced suites that crowd out CareStack, especially in mid-market deals where CareStack lacks hardware-attached economics.
weakness.headline: Entrenched incumbents can bundle to undercut CareStack

weakness.details: AI phone systems, AI documentation, and AI imaging are increasingly commoditized capabilities offered by horizontal players (e.g., generic AI scribe vendors, telephony AI platforms). If competitors can deliver similar AI functionality with lower switching cost, CareStack's premium positioning and proprietary AI moat could narrow, pressuring pricing power and renewal economics.
weakness.headline: AI feature commoditization erodes differentiation

weakness.details: As private equity rolls up dental practices into mega-DSOs, procurement increasingly favors platforms with the deepest integration across clinical, billing, imaging, and patient engagement — often from a single strategic vendor. If CareStack loses marquee DSO wins to incumbents or PE-backed consolidator platforms, its top-of-funnel enterprise pipeline could weaken.
weakness.headline: DSO roll-ups favor vertically integrated platforms over best-of-breed

weakness.details: CareStack operates with 1,300+ employees across US, UK, and India, including three engineering centers. With limited disclosed revenue and the most recent priced round dating to April 2021, the path to profitability and any potential need for fresh capital — including the possibility of a down round or restructuring — represents an execution and valuation overhang for new investors.
weakness.headline: Capital intensity with 1,300+ employees outpaces disclosed revenue visibility

weakness.details: CareStack's commercial presence is concentrated in the US, UK, and Australia. Regulatory divergence (NHS in UK, Australian dental scheme rules, US HIPAA/state laws) and the absence of meaningful operations in larger markets (Canada, Germany, France, Japan, Brazil) limits near-term TAM expansion and creates dependency on the dental economic cycles of these three specific geographies.
weakness.headline: Geographic concentration in three markets caps near-term growth ceiling

competitive_moat.details: CareStack's seven-module Enhanced Growth Solutions suite (VoiceStack, Aeka, CS Pay, ACE DSN, CareRevenue, VirtualAssistant, CS Membership) is natively integrated into the PMS, and Espire Dental alone has run 27,000,000+ API calls against the open API to consolidate data from multiple systems, signaling deep integration stickiness.

Practice data, clinical templates, recall logic, and multi-location workflows are deeply embedded over years of use; the company cites "days in A/R dropped 30%+" and "90% staff retention driven by ease of learning," framing migration cost rather than feature parity as the retention lever.

Proprietary branded AI modules (VoiceStack, Aeka, AI Suite) and a commissioned Forrester Total Economic Impact study documenting 6-month payback and up to $1.3M profit uplift for a 10-location composite over 3 years provide defensible, third-party-validated brand and methodology assets.

Healthcare-data compliance posture (HIPAA, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001:2022, GDPR) is a precondition for selling to enterprise DSOs and NHS practices; competitors without this certification stack face meaningful procurement friction.

3,000+ US practices, 500+ UK practices, and 2,000+ Australian dentists feeding 25,000+ active users generate a benchmarking and predictive-analytics dataset that strengthens product recommendations and AI tuning over time.

Dedicated enterprise field-sales teams in the US, UK, and Australia with localized phone numbers (+1, +44, +61), the Inner Circle flagship conference drawing 650+ dental professionals, and a CareStack Champions community are dedicated acquisition assets not easily replicated by greenfield entrants.

Cloud-native architecture (Microsoft Azure) with no expensive server upgrades or ongoing maintenance, and a Trivandrum/Kochi/Bangalore engineering footprint, support a structurally lower cost-to-serve versus legacy on-premise PMS vendors being displaced.

key_risks.details: All of CareStack's customer base, revenue, and product is concentrated in dental practice management. Downturns in dental procedure volumes, insurance reimbursement cuts, or macroeconomic pressure on discretionary dental spend (e.g., cosmetics, implants) directly compress the customer base's willingness to pay and ability to grow, with no diversification cushion.
key_risks.headline: Vertical concentration entirely in dental creates exposure to dental industry cyclicality and reimbursement pressure

key_risks.details: CareStack competes against deeply entrenched players such as Henry Schein One (Dentrix), Patterson (Eaglesoft), Curve Dental, Planet DDS (Denticon), and Open Dental. Incumbents benefit from decades of installed base, distribution scale, and bundled product offerings that can undercut CareStack's land-and-expand motion.
key_risks.headline: Highly competitive market against entrenched incumbents with deeper distribution

key_risks.details: Public information identifies only co-founders Mark Huzyak and Abilash Krishna (CEO), plus a Chairman (Babu Sivadasan) and a VP of Operations & Finance. No disclosed CFO, CRO, CTO, or other C-suite depth, which represents key-person dependency risk and execution risk as the company scales internationally and into larger enterprise accounts.
key_risks.headline: Limited disclosed executive bench beyond the two co-founders

key_risks.details: CareStack depends on integrations with Carestream, Dexis, Apteryx, Dolphin, DTX Studio, Adyen, DentalXChange, DoseSpot, Birdeye, and others for a complete product experience. Disruption, deprecation, or pricing changes by these partners could materially affect product functionality and customer satisfaction.
key_risks.headline: Reliance on third-party integrations (imaging, payments, e-prescribe, RCM) creates dependency and switching friction

key_risks.details: The most recent fully disclosed priced round is $22.5M in April 2021, with a subsequent Straumann investment in July 2022 of undisclosed size. While $145M cumulative is reported, current cash position, burn rate, and runway are not disclosed. With 1,300+ employees globally (including India engineering), operating cost is substantial, making the absence of recent disclosed metrics a meaningful visibility gap.
key_risks.headline: Public funding signals are stale; capital efficiency and runway trajectory are opaque

key_risks.details: CareStack uses a quote-based pricing model with no publicly disclosed tiers or starting prices. While this enables enterprise flexibility, it adds friction for SMB and mid-market prospects who expect transparent SaaS pricing, potentially increasing sales cycle length and customer acquisition cost in the smaller end of the market.
key_risks.headline: Pricing is opaque and quote-based, which can slow mid-market sales cycles

key_highlights.details: CareStack reports 3,000+ dental practices using its platform in the US market, 25,000+ active users, and 2,000+ dentists across the US. This level of customer base is meaningful scale for a vertical SaaS in dentistry.
key_highlights.headline: Large-scale dental practice management platform serving 3,000+ practices and 25,000+ users

key_highlights.details: CareStack has raised over $145M from leading institutions and strategic dental partners. Notable investors include Straumann (strategic in July 2022), Accel, Delta Dental, Eight Roads Ventures, F-Prime, and Steadview Capital. The Straumann relationship is particularly strategic given Straumann's deep presence in dental.
key_highlights.headline: Significant capital base with $145M raised from top-tier investors including Straumann

key_highlights.details: A Forrester Total Economic Impact study validated that CareStack pays for itself within 6 months, with profits increasing up to $1.3M and $280K in system consolidation savings for a composite 10-location organization over 3 years. This third-party validation is a strong enterprise sales asset.
key_highlights.headline: Forrester-validated ROI with 6-month payback and $1.3M profit uplift for 10-location practices

key_highlights.details: CareStack holds HIPAA, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001:2022, and GDPR certifications, providing it with the compliance posture needed to sell into large health systems, DSOs, and EU/UK regulated buyers.
key_highlights.headline: Enterprise-grade security and compliance stack: HIPAA, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, GDPR

key_highlights.details: CareStack has built proprietary AI capabilities including VoiceStack (24/7 AI phone system with intent understanding and natural language) and Aeka (AI-powered enterprise imaging), plus AI-assisted clinical documentation. These are integrated rather than third-party bolt-ons.
key_highlights.headline: Proprietary AI suite with native VoiceStack telephony and Aeka imaging modules

key_highlights.details: Documented outcomes include 190% increase in monthly insurance collections (Dental Depot), 75% increase in practice production (Dentcare Now), 40% reduction in A/R days (Plum Dental), 30% increase in collections without adding staff (Element Dental), and 90% staff retention (Alpha Dental).
key_highlights.headline: Strong, quantified customer outcomes across diverse practice types

key_highlights.details: Beyond US HQ in Celebration, FL, CareStack operates sales/support in London (UK, 500+ practices), Sydney (Australia, 2,000+ dentists), and engineering centers in Trivandrum, Kochi, and Bangalore. Localized UK NHS modules and Australian compliance widen addressable market.
key_highlights.headline: Multi-geography operations with localized presence in US, UK, and Australia

customer_concentration.details: Named enterprise and mid-market logos are widely distributed across DSOs, specialty practices, and SMB segments — including Espire Dental (30+ locations, 27M+ API calls), Dental Depot, Alpha Dental, MI Smiles, Enable Dental, Plum Dental, Element Dental, Root Periodontal, Kids Tooth Team, and several UK and Australian operators — with no single customer appearing to dominate public-facing materials. The quote-based, annual subscription model layered with add-on modules means DSO contracts contribute disproportionate revenue per logo, so a modest number of 30+ location DSOs likely drive significant ARR even though the customer count exceeds 3,000 in the US alone. Geographic diversification across the US, UK (500+ practices), and Australia (2,000+ dentists) reduces single-region churn exposure. Vertical specialization in dental keeps the customer base narrow but large-logos-spread, supporting a Moderate classification rather than High — concentration risk is real for a handful of multi-location DSOs but is buffered by deep SMB tail and multi-region footprint.

launches.full_text:
Planet DDS Marks Mid-Year Growth with Expanded AI Agent Suite and New Platform Packaging

Share

Enterprise wins, five new suites, and a growing bench of AI agents signal where dental software is headed

IRVINE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Planet DDS today shared mid-year results that reflect the market's growing confidence in its approach. Year-over-year ARR growth for its core solution, Denticon, reached 24.3%, cementing its position as the standard for growth-focused dental organizations. Momentum was driven in part by significant new enterprise wins, including Coast Dental (88 locations), Jefferson Dental (60 locations), Mosaic Dental Collective (47 locations), and Orthodontic Partners (62 locations). “Growth like this comes from solving a real problem: DSOs are tired of paying for complexity instead of results. Our job is to give them one platform that scales with them and AI that lightens the load on their teams. These results tell us we're building the right thing,” said Eric Giesecke, Chief Executive Officer of Planet DDS. A Growing Suite of AI Agents Planet DDS continues building out its AI agent suite with the industry's staffing shortage squarely in mind. The Confirmation Agent and Recall Agent handle patient confirmations and recall outreach automatically across every location. Earlier in August, Planet DDS launched two additional agents: Missed Appointment Rescheduling Agent recovers chair time lost to no-shows using an empathetic, non-accusatory outreach approach, and Cancellation Rescheduling Agent works the cancelled-appointment list to rebook the slot before the chair goes cold. Introducing DentalOS® Add-On Suites Alongside its agent expansion, Planet DDS is introducing a new way for practices to access the platform's growing capabilities. DentalOS® now serves as the base platform, with five add-on suites practices can pick and choose from based on what they actually need: Agents+, Clinical Voice+, Imaging+, Patient+, and Payments+. A DSO only pays for the suites it uses. Once a DSO adds a suite, every capability inside it, current and future, comes with it at no additional cost. A practice on Clinical Voice+, for example, gets every clinical documentation tool Planet DDS has released and will release, from AI Voice Perio to AI Voice Restorative Charting, without needing to evaluate and purchase each one separately. This flexible pricing means a group only pays for the suites it uses. "Customers want the flexibility to invest in the tools that matter most to their DSO, and the confidence that value keeps showing up inside the suites they've already chosen," said Nathan James, Chief Product Officer of Planet DDS. “DSOs end up managing fragmented systems, disconnected point solutions, and piecemeal pricing right when they're trying to scale,” said Nathan James, Chief Product Officer at Planet DDS. “We want DSOs to have real control over their investment instead. Suites let every group build a platform that matches what they actually do, and as we keep shipping new features inside each suite, that investment keeps paying off without any extra purchasing decisions on their end.” Partnerships and Community Growth Planet DDS's open ecosystem has grown to more than 80 signed integration partners, giving DSOs the flexibility to connect the tools they already rely on without leaving the platform. Among these, the Planet DDS partnership with Microsoft has become a key piece of how the company supports enterprise IT infrastructure for large DSOs, helping standardize security, identity management, and system reliability across every location on the platform. In May, Planet DDS co-hosted the inaugural Dental Capital Forum in New York City alongside Aquiline Capital Partners, Dykema, and West Monroe, an invitation-only gathering of dental investors, DSO leaders, and advisors that was well-received enough that the founding partners are already planning to make it an annual event. This February, the company also held Orbit, its annual Leadership & User Summit, drawing more than 500 attendees to Scottsdale, Arizona for over thirty sessions on RCM, clinical workflows, AI applications, and executive leadership. Orbit returns March 31 to April 3, 2027, with a new executive track, a golf tournament, and expanded content. Planet DDS also continued building out its education platforms in the first half of the year, including The Dental Economist Show (130+ episodes since 2024), The Morning Grind newsletter (40+ issues since 2025), and its 2026 Mid-Year Dental Industry Outlook Report, released in July. Recognition Additionally, Planet DDS's momentum has been reflected in a run of recent industry recognition: Inc. Regionals: #68 on the list, reflecting 93% two-year growth

launches.full_text:
Planet DDS Declares the Practice Management Era Over and Launches DentalOS®, the Dental Enterprise Platform for DSOs

Share

One Patient. One Schedule. One RCM.

IRVINE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Planet DDS today declared the practice management era in dental software over and launched DentalOS®, the dental enterprise platform built to replace it. DentalOS is not a smarter practice management system. It is a new category of software entirely: a unified platform that connects Denticon and Cloud 9 on a single data layer, with a new suite of enterprise capabilities, including AI agents, built on top. DentalOS will be available at no additional cost to Planet DDS customers, giving dental group executives visibility, control, and financial performance to run the organizations they’ve built. More than half of the largest 60 DSOs in North America already run on Planet DDS. What the company sees across the industry is consistent: multi-location enterprises using software built for a single practice. The company has observed the industry entering a new enterprise era, which requires a fundamentally different kind of software. “Every bet we’ve made as a company, we made early and often alone. Cloud-native before it was obvious, open ecosystem to give our customers choices, and enterprise-grade before DSOs were a mainstream conversation. It was never luck or prophecy. Our customers knew and we had the conviction to listen. DentalOS is our answer to the dental enterprise era,” said Eric Giesecke, CEO of Planet DDS. Why Planet DDS Built DentalOS Years of consolidation produced organizations managing dozens or hundreds of locations, with private equity-grade reporting requirements, multi-specialty complexity, and the operational ambition to run it all as one. The practice management software those organizations are running was only ever designed to manage a single office. “I’ve never met a DSO leader who said their biggest problem was finding the right practice management software. They talk about visibility, scale, AI, and operational consistency across dozens of locations. They’re looking for a platform that matches the ambition of what they’ve built,” said Mike Huffaker, Chief Revenue Officer of Planet DDS. Four forces are converging to make the status quo increasingly untenable: the industry-wide shift from acquisition to operation as DSOs focus on running what they’ve acquired; the arrival of AI, where the underlying data layer determines who wins; a labor crisis that makes automation a survival necessity; and a rising bar for enterprise-grade security, total cost of ownership, and visibility across multi-location dental organizations. “Every capability we're building—AI agents, clinical voice, predictive revenue cycle—performs relative to the quality of the data beneath it. DentalOS is that foundational platform. We built the platform so that everything built on it today and in the future performs at a level disconnected tools never could,” said Nathan James, Chief Product Officer of Planet DDS. What Is DentalOS? The Dental Enterprise Platform Explained DentalOS is the dental enterprise platform that connects practice management, revenue cycle, imaging, and AI on a single data layer for DSOs and multi-location dental groups. Built on an open ecosystem of 80+ integration partners, DentalOS gives operators the tools that fit their organization—not the tools a single vendor chose for them. On that foundation is a new layer of enterprise add-on suites, each solving specific operational problems at scale: Agents+ : Expands operational capacity without adding headcount. The Confirmation Agent automatically confirms appointments and updates the schedule; the Recall Agent identifies overdue patients and reaches out to book recall appointments. Both are available today. Coming soon: the Cancellation Recovery Agent, which rebooks cancelled appointments, and the Missed Appointment Recovery Agent, which follows up immediately with no-shows. RCM and clinical agents to come.

For a 20-provider group, that’s millions in recoverable revenue. The RCM Hub changes that—purpose-built for revenue cycle within DentalOS, not as an afterthought inside practice management, surfacing that risk before it becomes a write-off across eligibility, claims, remittance, and patient AR. DentalOS Phases: What's Launching and What's Coming DentalOS will launch in phases. Phase 1 establishes the enterprise foundation that makes everything else possible: a unified OS Desktop experience, enterprise-grade security with Single Sign On (SSO) and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), centralized user management, and an Agentic Marketplace for AI-powered workflows. This is the infrastructure layer that gives CTOs and IT teams the visibility and enterprise-level control they’ve been asking for. The platform roadmap ahead is persona-driven, with each phase designed to solve for a distinct role inside the DSO, from the front desk and DSO administrators to multi-specialty operators and enterprise leadership. Near-term phases focus on eliminating workflow friction and login fragmentation that costs staff time every day. Upcoming phases connect the multi-specialty enterprise and give leadership centralized control across every location and every user. DentalOS for Every Stage of DSO Growth Planet DDS is clear that the dental enterprise era is defined by intent, not size. A dental group that makes the right infrastructure decision at 15 locations will be better positioned at 150 than one that waits. For qualifying 2 to 9 location groups, the company’s Launchpad program gives early-stage groups access to the same DentalOS platform as the largest DSOs in the country. The long-term destination: a dental enterprise where the platform handles the operational noise, RCM friction approaches zero, every specialty is connected, and the data accumulated across every location and patient relationship becomes a measurable, compounding competitive advantage. launches.title: Dental Launch Radar: Mid-March 2026
launches.ai_summary: Three new dental technology products were launched in mid-March 2026, including OsteoGen's Bioactive Crystal Technology for bone grafting and Planet DDS's AI agents for practice management. SciCan also introduced the HYDRIM 112W G4+, an automated instrument washer featuring smart monitoring capabilities to enhance infection control and efficiency.
launches.author: Sarah Butkovic
launches.full_text:
Industry News Dental Launch Radar: Mid-March 2026 Three new product launches—a bioactive bone graft, alternative to AI front-office agents, and a smart instrument washer—signal how rapidly dental technology is reshaping clinical care and practice work.



Alternative material challenges current regenerative dentistry standard Bioactivity influences many restorative procedures and products when it comes to the rapidly evolving regenerative dental industry. Right now, sintered ceramics make up a large portion of today’s bone graft substitutes. The process invovles fusing particles into dense, ceramic structures to simulate natural bone via high heat.1 OsteoGen’s Bioactive Crystal Technology (BCT) is taking a different approach by forgoing sintering in favor of calcium phosphate crystals comprised of bone-like materials. The company says that circumventing the sintering process allows these crystals to retain bioactive properties because they are not exposed to the high sintering temperatures. The material releases calcium ions that may support osteoblastic differentiation and mineralized matrix deposition during healing. Cited by OsteoGen in their press release, research published in the Journal of Periodontology notes that BCT has 94.4% porosity, which may promote bone formation. The same study also found that BCT has a proliferation rate that is six times greater than xenograft and allograft materials.1 OsteoGen says the goal of this product is to shorten procedure time and simplify the bone grafting process without compromising solid clinical results.1 Bioactive Crystal Technology (BCT) AI workforce taking on front-office tasks Planet DDS, a dental software solutions company, has developed AI-powered workers to streamline front office work for staff members. According to Planet DDS, their AI agents can access live patient data, office schedules, and established workflows and are compatible with dental practice management software (Denticon and Cloud 9).2 The scheduling agent: Reaches out to patients from recall lists, waitlists, and those with unscheduled treatment Fills open schedule time when patients cancel appointments Books appointments Logs each interaction into Denticon or Cloud 9 The confirmation agent: Automates appointment confirmations Verifies patient identity before sharing protected health information Writes confirmation and reschedule outcome In a press release, CEO of Planet DDS Eric Giesecke said these tools are intended to increase practice productivity and relieve team members of time-consuming tasks and help them avoid routine busywork. He said: “DSOs that are scaling face an inherent tension—more locations mean more operational complexity, more communication to manage, and more pressure on teams already stretched thin ... [DentalOS] works alongside human teams so organizations can scale without sacrificing consistency, responsiveness, or the people who make it all work.”2 Instrument washer adds digital monitoring features Infection control company SciCan has debuted an automated instrument washer with a touch screen, LED lights, and customizable features—known as HYDRIM 112W G4+. According to SciCan's website, this model is designed to: Reduce the risk of sharps injuries by minimizing how much you’re handling your instruments Cut instrument cleaning costs by $10,000 a year Allow for more time chairside Clean more instruments per cycle than other washers on the market today The manufacturer notes this instrument washer includes smart technology to keep dental practices running smoothly. It has a touch-screen interface with on-screen instruction tutorials, connectivity to equipment software myCOLTENE, support for troubleshooting and running diagnostics, and a digital log of each cleaning cycle.3 SciCan reports the washer can remove 99.9% of protein residues under tested conditions.3 HYDRIM 112W G4+ instrument washer References: Bioactive Crystal Technology (BCT): the science behind predictable bone regeneration. Planet DDS Unveils DentalOS™ AI Agents: A New AI Workforce for Dental Operations

Share

Early access waitlist now open for purpose-built AI agents that connect directly to Denticon and Cloud 9.

IRVINE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Planet DDS today unveiled DentalOS™ AI Agents, a new category of AI-powered workers purpose-built to operate within the dental practice management system. DentalOS AI Agents are intelligent, autonomous agents that live inside Denticon and Cloud 9, accessing live patient data, real schedules, and established workflows to complete operational work the way a trained team member would, at any hour, across every location. The first agents target front desk operations, where missed communication directly leads to lost revenue. Today, the average dental practice sees a 15% no-show rate, costing providers more than $150,000 per year in lost production—and 36% of patients who miss appointments say they simply forgot. For DSOs and multi-location groups, these gaps compound across dozens or hundreds of locations. These are solvable problems. The newly announced Confirmation Agent and Scheduling Agent are designed to address these challenges systematically across organizations. But the front desk is only the starting point. Planet DDS will introduce additional AI agent roles throughout 2026 and beyond, building toward a full AI workforce spanning clinical coordination, patient communications, revenue cycle management, and more, all embedded within DentalOS. Denticon and Cloud 9 customers can join the early access waitlist at planetdds.com/ai-agents-early-access. “DSOs that are scaling face an inherent tension—more locations mean more operational complexity, more communication to manage, and more pressure on teams already stretched thin," said Eric Giesecke, CEO of Planet DDS. "We're introducing an entirely new way of using our software by providing access to an AI workforce that lives inside DentalOS, understands the full context of every patient interaction, and works alongside human teams so organizations can scale without sacrificing consistency, responsiveness, or the people who make it all work. The Confirmation and Scheduling Agents we're launching are just the beginning.” Meet the First Two AI Agents for Dental Front Desk Operations Confirmation Agent automates outbound appointment confirmations within a configurable window, helping DSOs reduce no-shows and stabilize provider schedules without increasing staff workload. If a patient can't make it, the agent can reschedule the appointment during the same call using policy-controlled slot search—without creating scheduling risk. It verifies patient identity before sharing protected health information, respects consent and office hours, and writes confirmation and reschedule outcomes back into Denticon and Cloud 9 with full auditability. The Confirmation Agent has been shown to increase appointment confirmation rates by 20–50% from historic baselines, reduce no-shows by 15–30%, and save front desk teams an estimated 60–75% of hours previously spent on manual confirmation workflows. Scheduling Agent keeps schedules full by proactively reaching out to patients from recall lists, waitlists, ASAP lists, and unscheduled treatment, then booking appointments directly into the practice management system. When cancellations occur, the agent triggers time-sensitive outreach to quickly recover open time. It reaches patients through outgoing calls and logs every interaction back into Denticon and Cloud 9, so teams maintain full visibility across locations. "The Confirmation and Scheduling Agents protect production and reduce no-shows, which for DSOs means healthier EBITDA," said Nathan James, Chief Product Officer at Planet DDS. "And this is just the first layer. As we bring AI agents into the revenue cycle, clinical coordination, and beyond, we're building a workforce that strengthens our customers’ business at every level.” How DentalOS AI Agents Work: Real-time access to live schedules and patient records within Denticon and Cloud 9

Independently complete front desk workflows, including appointment confirmations, rescheduling, missed call recovery, and routine patient inquiries

Natural patient communication that follows each organization's scheduling preferences and escalation paths

Operate simultaneously across the organization—configurable by location—while honoring each office’s working hours, holidays, and closures.

Intelligent escalation to human staff when clinical judgment or personal attention is needed Organizations retain full control over timing, task scope, and escalation rules—ensuring agents operate as a seamless extension of the team. Every DentalOS AI Agent—current and future—connects directly with Denticon and Cloud 9, cloud-based dental practice management platforms by Planet DDS, with real-time access to the same data and workflows human teams rely on every day. This shared foundation enables agents to act with full operational awareness, following each organization's scheduling rules, communication standards, and escalation paths without manual configuration for every interaction. It is also what makes the AI workforce scalable. As Planet DDS introduces new agents across additional operational domains, each will inherit the same data and organizational intelligence, allowing DSOs to continue expanding their AI workforce. Early Access Waitlist Now Open Planet DDS is opening an early access waitlist for DentalOS AI Agents to Denticon and Cloud 9 customers. Organizations on the waitlist will be among the first to deploy the Confirmation Agent and Scheduling Agent and help shape the future of AI-powered dental operations. To join the early access waitlist or learn more, visit planetdds.com/ai-agents-early-access. Resources Learn more about DentalOS AI Agents.

Discover Denticon Practice Management.

Explore Cloud 9 Ortho Practice Management.

Access the latest insights on dental technology and AI. About Planet DDS Dental software is broken. We aim to fix it. As a partner in growth for DSOs and dental groups outgrowing legacy systems and fragmented tools, Planet DDS delivers a cloud-based AI platform designed to scale alongside growing organizations. Powered by DentalOS™ with AI, Planet DDS is built on connection—connecting people, partners, and technology across an open ecosystem that includes Denticon Practice Management, Cloud 9 Ortho Practice Management, and Apteryx Cloud Imaging. Trusted by leading DSOs and emerging dental groups nationwide, Planet DDS supports more 100+ location DSOs than any other cloud-based dental practice management provider, enabling 14,500 practices and 175,000 users to move beyond outdated legacy software with seamless integrations, optimized workflows, and scalable technology built for growth.

In-Depth Examination of Segments, Industry Trends, and Key Competitors in the Dental Service Organization Market Dental Service Organization Market The dental service organization sector is poised for significant expansion in the coming years as it adapts to technological advancements and changing healthcare demands. This growth is supported by increasing consolidation in dental practices and the adoption of innovative platforms designed to enhance patient care and operational efficiency. Let's explore the market's current scale, key drivers, leading players, emerging trends, and segment highlights shaping this evolving industry.



Projected Growth and Valuation of the Dental Service Organization Market

The dental service organization market is expected to experience rapid growth, reaching a valuation of $379.41 billion by 2030. This forecast is based on a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 15.8%. Several factors contribute to this surge, including the ongoing consolidation of dental practices into larger networks and the rising demand for scalable, integrated dental service platforms. Additionally, the growing use of tele-dentistry services and data-driven strategies for patient acquisition are further fueling market expansion. The integration of AI-based diagnostic tools also plays a crucial role in enhancing both patient outcomes and operational processes.



Download a free sample of the dental service organization market report:

https://www.thebusinessresearchcompany.com/sample.aspx?id=33086&type=smp&utm_source=OpenPR&utm_medium=Paid&utm_campaign=Feb_PR



What Is Driving the Dental Service Organization Market Expansion

One major influence behind the market's growth is the increasing shift toward centralized practice management models. This approach allows for better coordination across multiple locations, providing streamlined workflows and improved patient experiences. Moreover, dental service organizations are embracing AI-driven systems for scheduling and billing, which reduce administrative burdens and optimize resource allocation.



Another important factor is the widespread adoption of digital patient records. These systems facilitate easier data sharing and integration across specialties, enabling multi-specialty dental networks to deliver comprehensive care. The emphasis on operational efficiency and standardization is helping organizations scale more effectively while maintaining high-quality services.



View the full dental service organization market report:

https://www.thebusinessresearchcompany.com/report/dental-service-organization-market-report?utm_source=OpenPR&utm_medium=Paid&utm_campaign=Feb_PR



Key Players Leading the Dental Service Organization Market

The dental service organization market features several prominent companies that dominate the space, such as Heartland Dental LLC, Aspen Dental Management Inc., Smile Brands Inc., Western Dental Services Inc., and Dental Care Alliance LLC. Other notable players include Great Expressions Dental Centers LLC, Dykema Gossett PLLC, Affordable Dentures & Implants LLC, MB2 Dental Solutions LLC, InterDent Service Corporation, Guardian Dentistry Partners LLC, Benevis LLC, Specialty1 Partners LLC, Pacific Dental Services LLC, Bluetree Dental LLC, iDental Group LLC, Affordable Care LLC, Lollipop Dental LLC, Straine Dental Management LLC, and Family Dental Care LLC.



Expanding Networks Through Strategic Partnerships

In June 2025, Innovate 32, a US-based dental services organization, partnered with Fort Bend Dental to broaden its affiliated practice network within Texas. This collaboration aims to strengthen their regional footprint, enhance operational support systems, and improve access to quality dental care by leveraging shared resources and centralized management. Fort Bend Dental is known for offering comprehensive oral healthcare services across the United States.



Technological Innovations Driving New Opportunities in the Market

Leading companies in the dental service organization market are prioritizing technological advancements, particularly the use of integrated cloud-based practice management platforms. These systems enable dental organizations to efficiently oversee multiple locations by consolidating administrative, financial, clinical, and patient engagement processes into one digital infrastructure. For example, in February 2024, US-based dental technology firm Planet DDS introduced Denticon Reimagined, an enhanced cloud platform designed specifically for large dental groups and DSOs. This platform boasts advanced analytics capabilities for real-time performance monitoring, built-in patient communication tools, and scalable architecture that supports centralized billing, scheduling, and reporting across numerous sites.



Major Segments Representing the Dental Service Organization Market

This market can be broken down into several key segments:

1) Type of Services: General Dentistry, Pediatric Dentistry, Orthodontics, Oral Maxillofacial Surgery, Periodontics, Cosmetic Dentistry, Endodontics, Prosthodontics

2) Practice Models: Single Specialty, Multi-Specialty, Corporate Owned, Independent Practitioner Networks, Franchise Models

3) Patient Demographics: Pediatric, Adult, Geriatric, Special Needs, Preventive Care Patients

4) Technology Utilization: Traditional Practices, Digital Records Management, Treatment Planning Software, Tele-dentistry, 3D Imaging and Printing, AI-Driven Diagnostics

5) End-Users: General Dentists, Dental Surgeons, and Specialists



Detailed Subsegments Within the Main Categories

The general dentistry segment includes services such as preventive dental care, routine exams, fillings and restorations, oral health education, and simple tooth extractions. Pediatric dentistry covers infant oral health, preventive care for children, restorative services, behavior management, and special needs care. Orthodontics features treatments like metal braces, ceramic braces, clear aligner therapy, lingual orthodontics, and early interceptive care. Oral maxillofacial surgery encompasses tooth extraction, implant surgery, corrective jaw surgery, trauma surgery, and oral pathology treatment. Periodontics involves gum disease treatment, scaling and root planing, periodontal surgery, gum grafting, and implant maintenance. Cosmetic dentistry includes teeth whitening, veneers, bonding, smile makeovers, and aesthetic contouring. Endodontics covers root canals, retreatment, apical surgery, trauma management, and pulp therapy. The prosthodontics segment includes crowns, bridges, complete and partial dentures, as well as implant-supported prosthetics.



This comprehensive breakdown highlights how the dental service organization market caters to a wide array of patient needs and utilizes advanced technologies to improve care delivery and operational efficiency.

Planet DDS Introduces AI Voice Perio to Bring Consistent, Scalable Perio Charting to DSOs

Share

The first AI and voice-powered perio system built into Denticon to ensure consistent, scalable clinical data for DSOs

IRVINE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Planet DDS today announced the launch of AI Voice Perio, the first voice-powered periodontal charting system built within Denticon. Designed specifically for DSOs and multi-location dental groups, this hands-free, voice-activated solution addresses a critical operational challenge: ensuring consistent, reliable perio data across locations without introducing fragmentation or operational overhead as organizations scale. AI Voice Perio captures periodontal measurements in real-time during the exam, eliminating the need for manual data entry and reducing interruptions. The system records voice commands directly into Denticon’s perio fields, ensuring reliable, consistent data that is stored automatically in patient records. “Scaling clinical operations without losing consistency is one of the hardest challenges DSOs face,” said Eric Giesecke, CEO of Planet DDS. “AI Voice Perio simplifies periodontal exams for clinicians and helps organizations capture consistent, reliable data as they grow. This gives clinical leaders standardized perio data they can trust for clinical oversight, training, and compliance.” The Future of Periodontal Exams By using a standardized voice-driven structure, AI Voice Perio ensures that exams are performed the same way each time, regardless of location or clinician. This results in comparable data over time, allowing DSOs to confidently build patient histories, track clinical trends, and maintain high-quality records as their practices grow. Key Features of AI Voice Perio: Voice-activated charting: Hygienists speak directly into Denticon’s system to record measurements, eliminating the need for manual typing or data entry. Built into Denticon: AI Voice Perio operates directly in Denticon’s clinical data model, ensuring consistency and governance without added reconciliation. Real-time corrections: Hygienists can make voice corrections during exams without interrupting the flow of the appointment. Standardized data capture: Ensures consistency in periodontal charting across practices, eliminating discrepancies caused by individual clinician preferences. Oral Health Report Cards: Results are saved in the patient record, providing longitudinal visibility of periodontal health. How AI Voice Perio Benefits DSOs DSOs and multi-location practices across the country are already experiencing the significant benefits of AI Voice Perio, with improved efficiency and consistency in their periodontal exams. “The feedback we’ve received on AI Voice Perio has been extremely positive. Adoption has been straightforward, and it makes periodontal exams easier,” said Etta Bourne, Vice President of System Integrations at Dental365. “It simplifies the workflow, allows hygienists to work more independently, and keeps everything in one system so they can stay focused on the patient instead of the process.” AI Voice Perio is now available to Denticon customers. Throughout 2026, Planet DDS will continue expanding its AI-powered clinical capabilities while working with partners across the DentalOS™ ecosystem to reduce operational complexity and improve care consistency as dental organizations scale. AutoEligibility brings DentalXChange’s real-time eligibility data natively into Denticon, helping front office teams save hours, prevent denials, and improve cash flow.

IRVINE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Planet DDS today announced the launch of AutoEligibility, a new native integration with DentalXChange that automates insurance eligibility checks directly inside Denticon, the leading cloud-based practice management platform for DSOs and group practices. With AutoEligibility, front-office teams can instantly see coverage details such as deductibles, waiting periods, and Medicaid eligibility. That means fewer denials, faster collections, and no time wasted on payer portals or phone calls. "What used to take our insurance verification team hours now happens seamlessly within Denticon,” said Barbara Maciel, Team Manager at GoDental Brands. “We currently have one person responsible for completing all insurance verifications for an entire office, and AutoEligibility has made the process so fast and efficient that one team member will now be able to support multiple offices. It’s helping us streamline our workflow, improve accuracy, and create a much better experience for our team, our patients, and our front office." Solving the Industry’s Costliest Administrative Bottleneck According to the Council for Affordable Quality Healthcare (CAQH) report, insurance verification accounts for nearly a quarter of all dental administrative transactions and remains the number one cause of claim delays and denials. AutoEligibility eliminates manual work by syncing coverage data directly through DentalXChange, giving staff immediate access to eligibility results within Denticon. With AutoEligibility, front-desk and billing teams can: Save 4 to 6 hours per office per day by automating eligibility checks.

Prevent denials before submission through complete coverage detail visibility.

Build patient trust with accurate, transparent cost estimates.

Standardize revenue cycle performance across every location. "Right now, one team member completes around 40 verifications per day, and with the implementation of AutoEligibility, we expect that number to double due to the speed and efficiency it brings to our processes,” added Maciel. Built for DSO Scale While some eligibility tools stop at a simple yes or no when checking coverage, AutoEligibility is designed for multi-location dental organizations that need accuracy, speed, and consistency across hundreds of offices. It brings together the reliability of DentalXChange’s payer connectivity and the scalability of Denticon’s native cloud architecture. “Eligibility verification is one of the biggest causes of lost revenue and wasted time in dentistry,” said Eric Giesecke, CEO of Planet DDS. “AutoEligibility eliminates that friction by automating verification across every location, every patient, every day. It’s faster, smarter, and far more accurate, helping practices protect cash flow and focus on care, not paperwork. With this launch, we’re taking another step toward our mission: Dental software is broken. We aim to fix it.” AutoEligibility is a part of the Planet DDS RCM Zero vision: Zero manual work. Zero denials. Zero wasted hours. By embedding real-time eligibility checks directly into Denticon, Planet DDS continues to streamline the revenue cycle, helping DSOs strengthen cash flow and deliver a smoother patient experience.
