expansion_highlight.description: DentalOS AI Agents launched February 2026 introduce a usage-based AI revenue layer ($0.25–$0.33/min) that expands wallet share inside the existing install base and converts one-time RCM savings into recurring per-minute ARPU.

Fifteen new AI partners onboarded in 2025 (Overjet, Pearl, VideaHealth, Dental Intelligence, Clerri, Vyne, DentalXChange) signal deliberate platformization, turning DentalOS into the integration hub for third-party AI and revenue-cycle vendors.

Launchpad Program offers 80% savings on cloud management and imaging for emerging dental groups with 2+ locations and $3M–$25M revenue, signaling intent to capture the mid-market and convert smaller DSOs before they scale into enterprise tier.

Track record of three acquisitions in 14 months (Legwork Dec 2021, QSIDental Aug 2022, Cloud 9 Jan 2023) combined with PE dry powder from the 2022 recapitalization indicates continued inorganic appetite for adjacent point solutions in imaging, ortho, and patient engagement.

Self-serve/PLG motion with $100 free credits on AI Agents and self-service MyTooth onboarding suggests the company is layering product-led growth on top of enterprise sales to lower acquisition cost for SMBs and emerging groups.

Vertical specialization into OSOs (orthodontic support organizations) via Cloud 9 and the Synchrony/CareCredit ortho-first integration opens a second specialty vertical beyond general dentistry DSOs, materially expanding TAM within the same sales motion.

company_assessment.market_position: Planet DDS is the leading provider of cloud-enabled dental practice management and dental imaging software in North America, serving over 13,000 dental practices across the U.S. Founded in 2003 and headquartered in Irvine, California, the company is privately held and PE-backed by Aquiline Capital Partners and Level Equity following a 2022 recapitalization. It serves dental service organizations (DSOs), orthodontic support organizations (OSOs), emerging dental groups, and independent practices, with notable customers including Dental Care Alliance, Sage Dental (140 locations), Coast Dental (88 locations), Smile Partners USA (120 locations), Jefferson Dental & Orthodontics (60+ locations), and Smile Brands. The company has pursued an aggressive acquisition strategy, acquiring Legwork (Dec 2021), QSIDental from NextGen Healthcare (Aug 2022), and Cloud 9 Software from Accel-KKR (Jan 2023).

strengths.details: AI Agents (Confirmation, Recall, upcoming RCM agents) are priced at $0.25-$0.33/min on usage-based billing, targeting the $150K+ per-provider annual revenue leakage from no-shows. Demonstrated outcomes of 15-30% no-show reduction and 4x+ ROI across 13,000+ practices suggest rapid adoption that can 2-3x revenue per existing customer within 24-36 months, with expanding agent catalog (clinical coordination, RCM) extending the wedge.
strengths.headline: AI agents unlock large usage-based revenue expansion per customer

strengths.details: Planet DDS has won flagship enterprise deals (Sage 140, Coast 88, Smile Partners 120, Jefferson 60+) by displacing Dentrix. As DSO consolidation continues, large groups standardize on a single platform, and Planet DDS's cloud-native architecture and proven multi-location conversion playbook (8 weeks per location, 60+ PMS migration experience) position it as the default choice, compounding ARR through upsell of additional modules.
strengths.headline: DSO consolidation tailwind cements preferred platform status

strengths.details: Unifying practice management, imaging, payments, patient engagement, financing (CareCredit), and AI agents on one platform - combined with deep integration to 100+ imaging sensors and 25+ third-party systems - generates significant workflow lock-in. Customer testimonials (e.g., 'we would never even consider going back') confirm stickiness, supporting NRR expansion and low gross churn.
strengths.headline: Vertical integration creates durable switching cost moat

strengths.details: Daily operational and clinical data flowing from 13,000+ practices trains increasingly accurate predictive models for revenue cycle, recall prioritization, and clinical decision support - assets smaller competitors cannot replicate. This data moat deepens as DentalOS AI Agents expand into clinical coordination and RCM, widening the gap versus legacy PMS vendors.
strengths.headline: Data network effects from 13,000+ practices compound AI advantage

strengths.details: Cloud 9 acquisition (Jan 2023) gave Planet DDS the only fully cloud-based orthodontic PMS, opening the OSO segment with 2,500+ orthodontic practices already on platform. CareCredit expansion reaches 17,500 combined dental/ortho practices. Specialty adjacencies (oral surgery, pediatric, perio) represent further TAM expansion on existing platform infrastructure.
strengths.headline: Adjacent segment expansion into orthodontics and specialty dentistry

weakness.details: Henry Schein One (backed by KKR/Blackstone) and Patterson Companies have meaningfully larger R&D budgets, distribution reach, and installed bases. As they roll out cloud and AI features to legacy Dentrix and Eaglesoft bases over the next 12-24 months, Planet DDS's AI differentiation compresses and customer displacement becomes harder, slowing new logo growth.
weakness.headline: Incumbent AI counterattack from Dentrix and Eaglesoft

weakness.details: Planet DDS's growth thesis depends on continued DSO consolidation and new DSO formation. If DSO roll-up activity slows due to higher interest rates, tighter dental financing, or reimbursement pressure, the pipeline of large enterprise deals that drive new ARR may compress, exposing the company to more competitive, slower-growth mid-market and SMB segments.
weakness.headline: DSO market maturation could slow the growth engine

weakness.details: With operations confined to the United States, total addressable market is limited to roughly 200K dental practices versus a global dental software TAM multiple times larger. Lack of international expansion roadmap means growth must come from share gains and ARPU expansion in a finite market, eventually requiring costly market entry investments.
weakness.headline: Geographic ceiling caps long-term TAM at ~200K U.S. practices

weakness.details: Denticon, Cloud 9, Apteryx, Legwork, and QSIDental each retain distinct codebases, user experiences, and brand identities despite the DentalOS vision. Fully unifying these platforms is a multi-year, capital-intensive undertaking; in the meantime, customers on older platforms experience slower feature parity, risking dissatisfaction and competitive defection.
weakness.headline: Integration debt from multiple acquired platforms

weakness.details: Aquiline Capital Partners and Level Equity recapitalized in June 2022, suggesting a likely liquidity event window in 2026-2029. A premature exit (secondary sale, dividend recap, or strategic sale at a cyclical valuation trough) could redirect management attention from product investment to exit optics, while also potentially introducing an unfriendly successor owner.
weakness.headline: PE exit timing may not maximize long-term value

competitive_moat.details: Deep cross-product integration across Denticon/Cloud 9 practice management, Apteryx imaging, Planet DDS Pay payments, MyTooth engagement, and DentalOS AI creates substantial switching costs; the company has migrated customers from over 60 legacy PMS systems and runs 8-week per-location conversion programs, indicating workflow depth that is costly to unwind.

100+ imaging sensor integrations (Carestream, Vatech, Sirona, Acteon, Tuxedo), 25+ third-party PMS/system integrations, and 15 onboarded AI partners (Overjet, Pearl, VideaHealth, Dental Intelligence, Clerri, Vyne, Weave) create a two-sided network effect where third parties build to Planet DDS standards rather than risk exclusion.

Data aggregated from 13,000+ practices (14,500+ Denticon practices alone) across scheduling, clinical, imaging, and revenue cycle workflows provides training fuel for DentalOS AI models, predictive analytics, and cross-location benchmarking that new entrants cannot replicate.

FDA-cleared AI imaging analysis (Apteryx), ISO 13485:2016/MDSAP medical device certification, SOC 2 Type 2, and HIPAA/HITECH compliance create regulatory-grade moats difficult for point-solution competitors to match, particularly for clinical-decision-support claims.

Dedicated enterprise field sales targeting DSO executives (CDOs, IT/Ops leaders) with consultative selling and structured multi-site rollouts, combined with ADSO industry participation and named-logo wins (Sage Dental 140 locations, Coast Dental 88 locations, Smile Partners USA 120 locations, Jefferson Dental 60+ locations), builds a defensible enterprise pipeline.

key_risks.details: Henry Schein One's Dentrix and Patterson's Eaglesoft hold the dominant positions in dental PMS with decades of distribution, training networks, and installed bases across hundreds of thousands of practices. Planet DDS must continue displacing legacy systems to grow, and incumbents are actively modernizing with cloud and AI features of their own.
key_risks.headline: Intense competition from entrenched incumbents with massive installed bases

key_risks.details: Operating geographies are restricted to the United States with no disclosed international expansion. The U.S. dental practice market (~200K practices) is significantly smaller than global dental markets, and the company has not articulated a credible international growth path.
key_risks.headline: Heavy concentration in the North American dental market limits TAM expansion

key_risks.details: Completed three major acquisitions in ~14 months (Legwork Dec 2021, QSIDental Aug 2022, Cloud 9 Jan 2023) plus earlier Apteryx deal. Managing Denticon, Cloud 9, Apteryx, Legwork, and QSIDental as distinct sub-brands creates technical debt, fragmented user experiences, and slower time-to-unified DentalOS vision than a natively built competitor.
key_risks.headline: Acquisition-driven growth creates integration and platform unification risk

key_risks.details: Sales motion is heavily skewed toward enterprise DSOs and OSOs of 100+ locations. DSO market consolidation, buyout cycles, or a slowdown in DSO roll-up activity (a key sales driver) could compress new logo growth; smaller private practices remain a secondary segment with lower ACVs.
key_risks.headline: Customer concentration in DSOs exposes revenue to DSO consolidation dynamics

key_risks.details: DentalOS AI Agents and Apteryx AI imaging are positioned as key differentiators, but AI imaging vendors (Pearl, Overjet, VideaHealth) are integrated with the platform AND sell standalone; incumbents like Dentrix Ascend are rolling out AI features, eroding the moat within 12-24 months.
key_risks.headline: AI differentiation is at risk of commoditization as competitors add similar capabilities

key_risks.details: Aquiline Capital Partners and Level Equity recapitalized in June 2022 and typically hold investments 4-7 years, implying a potential exit event (secondary sale, IPO, or strategic M&A) in the 2026-2029 window. PE exit timing may not align with maximum value creation, and management bandwidth may be diverted to exit preparation.
key_risks.headline: PE ownership timing could pressure strategic decisions

key_highlights.details: Planet DDS serves over 13,000 dental practices via Denticon (14,500+ practices per platform data) plus 2,500+ orthodontic practices via Cloud 9, with 15,000+ dental practices reachable through the Synchrony CareCredit integration, giving it one of the largest footprints in dental software.
key_highlights.headline: Industry-leading scale with 13,000+ practices served across North America

key_highlights.details: DentalOS with AI launched as the industry's first AI-native platform for enterprise DSOs, embedding AI across revenue cycle, imaging, orthodontics, and patient engagement. AI Agents (Confirmation, Recall) deliver 15-30% no-show reduction, 20-50% increase in confirmations, 60-75% reduction in manual outreach hours, and 4x+ ROI at $0.25-$0.33/min usage pricing.
key_highlights.headline: First AI-native dental platform with autonomous AI agents delivering measurable ROI

key_highlights.details: Single platform includes Denticon (general dentistry PMS), Cloud 9 (ortho PMS), Apteryx XVWeb (FDA-cleared AI imaging), Planet DDS Pay (payment processing), and MyTooth (patient engagement), backed by 100+ sensor integrations, 25+ third-party system integrations, and migration experience from 60+ legacy PMS systems.
key_highlights.headline: Comprehensive integrated platform spans PM, imaging, payments, and engagement

key_highlights.details: Completed a recapitalization with Aquiline Capital Partners (lead) and Level Equity in June 2022, supporting an aggressive acquisition strategy (Legwork, QSIDental, Cloud 9) and product investment that has driven inclusion on the 2023 Deloitte Technology Fast 500 and 2025 Inc. 5000.
key_highlights.headline: Backed by top-tier PE sponsors (Aquiline Capital Partners, Level Equity)

key_highlights.details: Major enterprise wins include Sage Dental (140 locations), Coast Dental (88 locations), Smile Partners USA (120 locations across multiple states), Jefferson Dental & Orthodontics (60+ locations), and Dental Care Alliance, demonstrating ability to displace legacy incumbents like Dentrix in large group settings.
key_highlights.headline: Strong enterprise DSO win track record with marquee multi-location customers

key_highlights.details: Holds SOC 2 Type 2 (organization-wide), ISO 13485:2016 and MDSAP certification for Apteryx XVWeb medical device quality management, and full HIPAA, ARRA, and HITECH compliance, satisfying procurement requirements of large DSOs and institutional buyers.
key_highlights.headline: Enterprise-grade compliance and security certifications across the portfolio

key_highlights.details: Recognized as ADSO Innovation Award 2025 winner, G2 Momentum Leader and Highest User Adoption in Dental Practice Management (Spring 2025), Inc. 5000 Fastest Growing Private Companies 2025, and Deloitte Technology Fast 500 (2023), providing strong third-party validation.
key_highlights.headline: Multiple industry awards validate market leadership position

customer_concentration.details: Customer base spans roughly 13,000–15,000 practices, materially reducing single-customer revenue risk; however, named enterprise DSOs are large by site count (Sage Dental 140, Smile Partners USA 120, Coast Dental 88, Jefferson Dental 60+) and represent meaningful ARR concentration in the top decile. Revenue is anchored to multi-year SaaS subscriptions plus usage-based AI consumption and transaction-fee payments, with no single logo disclosed as exceeding low double-digit revenue share. Net concentration risk is Moderate: enterprise logos elevate churn impact per account but the long tail of mid-market and emerging groups diversifies the base and aligns pricing to recurring, contractually sticky workflows.

launches.author: Business Wire
launches.full_text:
Weave and CareCredit Go Live with Integration That Places Patient Financing Inside the Front-Office Workflow
LEHI, Utah, October 12, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Weave (NYSE: WEAV), a leading AI-powered patient communications and payments platform purpose-built for healthcare practices, today announced the live availability of its integration with CareCredit, a leading patient financing solution from Synchrony (NYSE: SYF). The integration gives front-office staff real-time visibility into a patient's financing options directly within Weave — bringing one of healthcare's hardest conversations forward, before the appointment begins.
For most patients, the question of how to pay comes last: after the exam, after the recommendation, often as a surprise at checkout. That timing has consequences. Out-of-pocket costs remain one of the most common reasons patients delay or decline treatment. By surfacing a patient's CareCredit status and available credit at the start of the visit, Weave replaces sticker shock with an informed conversation — and gives practices a way to solve cost alongside the patient rather than let it stand between them and care.
It's also the latest expression of Weave's single-system approach: financing no longer lives in a separate portal, but inside the workflow where the front office already works.
"Affordability is one of the defining challenges facing patients, and practices are navigating shrinking margins at the same time," said Marcus Bertilson, Chief Operating Officer at Weave. "By making CareCredit a native part of the front-office experience, we're giving practices the tools to meet patients where they are financially — and to move more care forward. When staff can see a patient's available credit before the appointment, cost stops being the obstacle and starts being part of the plan."
Key benefits of the integration include:
-
The financial conversation, moved up front. Staff can view a patient's CareCredit status and available credit directly within Weave — no switching between systems.
-
CareCredit helps broaden access to recommended treatment. Promotional financing options help more patients confidently move forward with the care they want or need.
-
Deeper payments adoption. 43% of recently surveyed Weave payments customers said they would use Weave's payment services exclusively once CareCredit is added.
-
A modern, mobile-first experience. Practices can initiate CareCredit payments in-office or via a text-to-pay link, and patients can apply for credit directly within Weave or on their own device — meeting patients where they already are.
"The Weave team has built a seamless experience for practices that want to offer CareCredit at the point of care," said Greg Pierce, SVP Network Solutions at Synchrony (CareCredit). "When financing options are visible earlier in the patient journey — at a moment when clearer options can make a real difference — practices can have more confident conversations, and more patients move forward with the treatment they need."

LEHI, Utah --(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Weave (NYSE: WEAV), a leading AI-powered patient engagement and payments platform purpose-built for healthcare practices, today announced a new authorized integration with Elation Health, a leading clinical platform for independent primary care. The integration reduces manual work and improves operational efficiency by connecting patient communication directly to the practice's electronic health record (EHR).

Independent and direct primary care practices often manage disconnected systems and manual processes that divert staff time from patient care. The Weave and Elation Health integration addresses that friction by automatically syncing patient and appointment data between the two platforms, creating a connected operational layer that automates communication across the patient journey.

Manual data entry remains a significant drain on practice staff. A recent Weave survey of dental practices found that 80% of staff spend at least 30 minutes a day on manual data entry, with more than a quarter losing two or more hours. The new integration can give that time back to primary care teams by eliminating manual CSV uploads and automatically syncing data between systems.

"Practices using Elation Health are focused on delivering personal, relationship-driven care, and that means their teams shouldn't be stuck managing software instead of patients. This integration can clear the way for staff to spend more of their time where it matters most," said Scott Chandler, VP of Strategic Partnerships at Weave.

With the integration, practices using both Weave and Elation Health can:

Automatically sync patient and appointment data between systems, removing the need for manual uploads.

Identify callers instantly with real-time Call Pop showing patient and appointment context.

Reduce no-shows with automated appointment reminders and two-way texting.

Write appointment confirmations back into Elation Health automatically.

Grow online reputation with automated review requests sent after completed appointments.

LEHI, Utah - Weave (NYSE:WEAV) announced Tuesday new platform features including single sign-on authentication, expanded AI receptionist capabilities, and automated insurance collection tools for healthcare practices.

The AI receptionist now allows practices to configure automated responses based on working hours and contact type, distinguish between new and existing patients, and set escalation protocols for staff handoffs. Text-based AI interactions integrate into the Weave inbox, and new analytics provide visibility into call-handling performance.

The platform’s automated insurance capture feature enables practices to collect insurance information remotely before appointments. The system runs eligibility reports and transfers verified data to patient charts in practice management systems, according to a press release statement.

Marcus Bertilson, Chief Operating Officer and Head of Product at Weave, said the updates address customer requests for security controls, AI performance visibility, and reduced manual work for front-office teams.

The company cited its 2026 State of Healthcare Pulse Survey, which found 47% of dental practices report staffing shortages. The survey also indicated 51% of practices want automated insurance verification and 40% want automated eligibility checks.

Weave provides a patient engagement and payments platform for healthcare practices and serves over 40,000 customer locations. The company, valued at $579 million, generated $249 million in revenue over the last twelve months with 17% year-over-year growth. According to [InvestingPro](https://www.investing.com/pro/WEAV) analysis, which tracks 1,400+ US equities with comprehensive metrics, Weave currently trades below its Fair Value and analysts forecast the company will turn profitable this year. The stock has delivered strong returns recently, gaining nearly 7% in the past week. The company was named a 2026 Best Software Awards winner for healthcare software products by G2.

New Weave product enhancements, an omnichannel AI Receptionist, and Automated Insurance Capture

Weave (NYSE: WEAV), a leading AI-powered patient engagement and payments platform purpose-built for healthcare practices, today announced a new set of platform capabilities designed to further meet the security, scalability, and automation needs of its growing enterprise customer base. The updates span single sign-on desktop authentication, expanded AI Receptionist functionality, and automated digital insurance collection, continuing Weave's investment in a platform that is as intelligent as it is easy to use.

"Enterprise practices need a platform that scales with them, securely and intelligently," said Marcus Bertilson, Chief Operating Officer and Head of Product at Weave. "These updates reflect what we hear consistently from our larger customers: they want stronger security controls, more visibility into AI performance, and less manual work for their front-office teams. We're building Weave to handle all three, without adding complexity for practices or patients."

Deliver Smarter Patient Interactions with AI Receptionist

According to Weave's 2026 State of Healthcare Pulse Survey, 47% of dental practices are experiencing staffing shortages, and the pressure to do more with existing teams has never been greater. Weave has significantly expanded its AI Receptionist capabilities, giving practices more control, visibility and automation across both calls and texts. Practices can now configure AI behavior based on working hours and contact type, distinguish between new and existing patients, and define escalation paths when a staff handoff is needed. Text-based AI interactions flow directly into the Weave inbox, preserving conversation context and keeping staff working in the tool they already use daily. New analytics give practice owners a clear view of call-handling performance and business impact, so no patient interaction goes untracked.

Simplify Patient Intake from Anywhere

In that same survey, automation is a priority, with 51% of practices wanting automated insurance verification, and 40% expressing the same for eligibility checks — yet both remain largely manual. Weave now enables practices to collect insurance information remotely ahead of the appointment. The platform automatically runs eligibility reports and writes verified insurance data back to the patient chart in the practice management system, eliminating the need for patients to be present and reducing the manual data entry that consumes hours of front-office time each day.

“What I hear from DSO leaders consistently is that they need technology that meets enterprise security standards, reduces operational drag across locations, and integrates AI in a way that's seamless and compliant. The direction Weave is taking with these updates reflects a real understanding of what these groups actually need to scale,” said Brian A. Colao, Director of Dykema's Dental Service Organizations Industry Group.

For more information, visit https://www.getweave.com/weave-enterprise/

About Weave

Weave is a leading vertical SaaS company delivering an AI-powered patient engagement and payments platform purpose-built for modern healthcare practices. More than software, Weave is an always-on teammate—handling patient interactions across voice and text and operating at the center of the patient journey. Through agentic AI workflows and authorized integrations with practice management systems, Weave ensures critical tasks like scheduling, insurance verification, and payments happen seamlessly, so nothing falls between the cracks. By embedding AI directly into daily operations, Weave reduces administrative workload, frees up staff to focus on human-centered care, and delivers real-time insights that help practices run smarter and grow with confidence. Serving over 40,000 customer locations, Weave was named a 2026 Best Software Awards winner for healthcare software products by G2. To learn more, visit getweave.com/newsroom.

launches.full_text: WeaveX Inc. (Headquarters: Shibuya, Tokyo, Representative Director: Ryo Toyazaki, hereinafter referred to as "WeaveX") will start providing its self-developed career design AI "LAife" and a team of experienced HR professionals, a human resources BPO service for small and venture companies called "LAife Align" (tentative name) from June 16, 2026. This service is a one-stop support model for small and growing companies that do not have the resources to hire dedicated HR strategic partners (HRBP), assisting from recruitment (requirement definition, document screening, interview support) to placement and development. HRBP is not a function needed only by large companies; rather, it plays a crucial role in supporting business growth for small and venture companies that are advancing recruitment, development, and organizational building with limited personnel. By combining ultra-fast data structuring by AI and professional insights (tacit knowledge from the field), we make it possible to implement advanced HR strategies, which were previously the privilege of large companies, in small and growing companies. Background: Intensifying recruitment market and the limits of "one-person HR" In the current situation, the importance of "investment in people (human capital management)" in companies has reached an all-time high due to the domestic labor shortage and the acceleration of reskilling policies. While large companies are rapidly advancing organizational redesign based on AI, small and venture companies, which need these benefits the most, are facing serious challenges such as the following. The limits of "one-person HR": A single person is responsible for recruitment, labor, and general affairs, and cannot manage HR strategies (HRBP functions) directly linked to management. Serious mismatches: Early departures are frequent due to "recruitment mismatches" arising from anxiety and lack of resources, leading to significant opportunity losses for companies and organizations, especially in key positions such as sales. To resolve the dilemma of "no resources but cannot compromise" faced by small ventures, we have launched a new co-pilot HR BPO service "LAife Align" (tentative name) that combines "AI productivity" and "professional field sense." Service Overview: "Next-generation HR co-pilot" realized by people (tacit knowledge) × AI (LAife) "LAife Align" (tentative name) is neither a service that sells SaaS nor a traditional task outsourcing BPO. It incorporates AI "LAife" into consulting/BPO support related to recruitment, placement, and development, enhancing the quality of our support while also allowing both companies and candidates to utilize it in some processes. Instead of providing AI as a separate product, we integrate it into the support process, fundamentally changing corporate HR decisions to be deeper and more reproducible, which is a decisive difference from traditional services. Our consultants and AI will formalize the "unarticulated requirements (tacit knowledge)" held by the management and field, while simultaneously structuring candidates' true feelings and thought processes as "line" data. By visualizing each other's tacit knowledge as data and organizing it as "company-specific HR assets" by our consultants, we eliminate discrepancies in recognition between management, HR, and the field, achieving the fastest possible organization building without mismatches. Specific support examples: Extraction of tacit knowledge: Our HR professionals and AI will interview to articulate the ideal candidate profile and challenges of the company. Structuring by AI: Candidates will use AI "LAife" to automatically profile values and thought processes from dialogue data. Organizing HR asset data: Extracted data will be analyzed by our consultants and delivered as "selection criteria and development plans that can be used on-site from tomorrow." Examples of outputs provided: Recruitment area: Phase-specific recruitment requirement definitions, document screening criteria based on data, interview support, 90-day onboarding plans. Placement and development area: Assignment proposals that match individual value data with business needs, individual growth themes, and mentor matching design. Competitive Advantage: "Ability to implement on-site" that cannot be imitated by generic AI tools We believe that a SaaS model that only provides tools cannot save the "on-site decision-making" of small companies. That is why WeaveX is thoroughly committed to "implementing on-site decision-making and practical workflows" that cannot be solved by AI alone. The value created by co-creation between people and AI, rather than differentiation of functions, is our greatest strength. Future Outlook: WeaveX aims to package the "successful model linking management, HR, and the field" created by this service into a unique AI product in the future, targeting horizontal expansion such as BPaaS. We aim to spread not just as a functional provider but as a new organizational development infrastructure that drives corporate growth autonomously. We will democratize advanced HR strategies (HRBP) for all companies towards the realization of our mission "to weave our own stories" and vision "a world where challenges are the norm." Comment from Representative Director Ryo Toyazaki: "HR is caught in the middle when the opinions of management and the field diverge. Candidates are judged solely by their resumes and do not get to show their true worth. I have seen such 'discrepancies where no one is happy' far too often in my previous job. That is why we want to use cutting-edge technology like AI to eliminate such 'misalignments between people and organizations.' The 'line' data woven from dialogue by AI will become a common language connecting management, HR, the field, and candidates. Small ventures can create strong organizations that do not lose to large companies, in a more human way than anywhere else—this is the world that our team will strive to realize together." About WeaveX Inc. Mission: To establish "weaving our own stories" as a permanent concept. Vision: To become a platformer of "a world where challenges are the norm." Representative Director: Ryo Toyazaki Location: 1-10-8 Dogenzaka, Shibuya, Tokyo Business Description: Career support business utilizing AI Corporate Website: https://weavex.jp/ Contact for this matter: WeaveX Inc. Public Relations Email: support@weavex.co.jp ▼ Event Information: [For those in their 20s and 30s] Community event "LAife Base" to be held on July 2. A community event "LAife Base" where young professionals can openly discuss their career options and values. Due to popular demand, the next event will be held on July 2 (Thursday)! Would you like to find peers with whom you can share your current concerns and future challenges openly? Date: July 2, 2026 (Thursday) 19:30-21:00 Target: Working professionals in their 20s to 30s Details & Registration: https://laifebase2.peatix.com/.

Weave Call Intelligence Helps Address Rising Care Deferral as Patients Delay Procedures Over Concerns About Affordability
Weave’s latest Call Intelligence capabilities help healthcare practices engage patients before cost concerns take over
LEHI, Utah--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Weave (NYSE: WEAV), a leading AI-powered patient communications and engagement platform purpose-built for healthcare practices, today announced a series of platform enhancements to one of its leading AI products, Call Intelligence. The latest updates turn the product from a robust analytics tool into a deeply embedded, AI-driven workflow engine for modern healthcare practices.
Healthcare businesses don't just need more data — they need to prioritize follow-up without drowning in more overhead.
Share
The announcement comes at a pivotal moment for the healthcare industry. According to recent polling, two-thirds of Americans (66%) say they worry about affording health care, ranking it higher than anxiety about utilities, food, housing, and gas. More than half of adults (55%) report their healthcare costs have increased in the past year, and 56% expect those costs to become even less affordable in the year ahead. Against this backdrop, the window between a patient's intent to schedule and their decision to defer care is narrowing — and every missed call, incomplete conversation, or overlooked follow-up now carries a greater cost for practice owners.
"Healthcare businesses don't just need more data — they need to prioritize follow-up without drowning in more overhead. Call Intelligence turns everyday interactions into meaningful, measurable outcomes that capture revenue and maintain the human touch,” said Abhi Sharma, Chief Technology Officer at Weave. “The refined version of Call Intelligence acts as an indispensable teammate that allows front-desk teams to focus more on their patients. In an environment marked by rising costs, patient trust and communication are everything."
Behaving more like an educated staff member than software, Weave’s Call Intelligence:
- Prioritizes high-value and urgent follow-ups. Opportunity detection helps practices identify unscheduled patients and track which appointments were recovered after an initially unscheduled interaction — giving leaders a clearer picture of scheduling conversion and ROI.
- Integrates workflows directly with practice management systems (PMS). With select PMS writebacks, Call Intelligence connects AI-generated summaries directly to the practice's system of record — reducing manual data entry, improving documentation consistency, and making conversation insights easier to operationalize without leaving existing workflows.
- Includes enterprise and multi-location capabilities. The product now supports the needs of larger practices and multi-location organizations with semantic search across conversation transcripts, multi-location comparison views, aggregated reporting, granular filtering, data exportability, and role-based access controls.
- Covers expanded verticals in healthcare: Originally launched with a dental focus, Call Intelligence now serves a growing range of healthcare verticals — including veterinary, optometry, and medical specialties such as dermatology, surgery, primary care, mental health, and plastic surgery.
"Before Call Intelligence, we had very limited insight into call quality, missed opportunities, or consistency across staff. Now we can review real call data and identify patterns that were previously invisible — missed conversion opportunities, inconsistent scripting, or staff not feeling empowered to use the tools at their disposal,” said dermatologist and multi-location owner, Dr. Jeffrey Ellis. “The result has been improved consistency across the team, and stronger conversion of inbound inquiries into booked appointments."

ADA Member Advantage endorses Weave as patient engagement platform

by Mary Beth Versaci

ADA Member Advantage has endorsed Weave to provide its artificial intelligence-powered patient communications and engagement platform to Association members.

Authorized integrations with practice management systems enable Weave to power practice operations such as scheduling, verification of insurance eligibility and payment collections. By embedding AI directly into practice workflows, Weave helps reduce administrative burden and delivers real-time insights.

Weave’s all-in-one platform includes the following tools:

• Customized phone system and number: Weave’s intelligent phone system equips the dental team with actionable insights on every call by displaying patient information up front. All calls and texts are unified under the practice’s trusted phone number to help ensure consistent, professional communication.

• Always-on AI receptionist: Weave’s AI-powered receptionist automatically follows up on missed calls with text messages that let patients schedule appointments, answers frequently asked questions in real time, and escalates to a staff member when needed.

• Faster insurance eligibility insights: Weave’s enhanced insurance tool leverages robotic process automation to access dental payer portals directly and retrieve detailed eligibility information. Dental teams gain a complete view of coverage, including frequency limitations, remaining benefits and code-specific details.

• Enterprise-grade infrastructure: Built for multi-location health care practices and dental support organizations, Weave Enterprise centralizes operations across dozens or hundreds of locations to standardize workflows, help improve efficiency and accelerate revenue cycle management.

"We are excited to launch this new relationship with Weave," said Allen Reavis, D.D.S., chair of the ADA Member Advantage board of directors. "They have a deep understanding of dentistry and what happens in the front office of a dental practice. This has led them to create a highly customer-focused suite of services that will help ADA members save time and improve efficiency within the many different aspects of patient communication."

Before making the endorsement, ADA Member Advantage conducted a vetting process on the effectiveness and value of Weave's solutions. Members who sign up receive discounts and enhanced training.

“Weave was built to improve practice operations so health care professionals can focus on patient care, and we’re proud to support ADA members with technology that can deliver those results,” said David McNeil, chief revenue officer at Weave. “To be selected through such a rigorous process underscores the real impact our platform is having in practices across the country.”

Weave Communications, Inc. Q4 2025 Earnings Call Summary - Moby Strategic Performance and Operational Context Achieved 17% year-over-year revenue growth in Q4, marking the 16th consecutive quarter of meeting or exceeding the high end of revenue guidance.

Performance was driven by strong adoption of payments and new location additions, particularly in the specialty medical vertical which saw record growth in Q4.

Management attributes their competitive advantage to a 'data moat' built on billions of patient interactions and authorized integrations with practice management systems that horizontal AI providers cannot replicate.

The platform is evolving from a communication tool into an 'orchestration layer' that treats patient interactions as single persistent threads across voice, text, and AI agents.

Strategic positioning focuses on capturing the practice's labor budget by automating administrative tasks like scheduling and billing, which are the largest components of SMB cost structures.

Gross margin reached a record 73.3%, driven by cloud infrastructure efficiencies and the amortization of older phone hardware and payment terminals.

The specialty medical vertical, currently at roughly 1% market penetration, is positioned as the primary growth engine due to its large addressable market and increasing integration depth. 2026 Strategic Roadmap and Guidance Assumptions Full-year 2026 revenue is projected between $273 million and $276 million, with growth expected to accelerate in the second half as new AI products reach general availability.

General availability of omnichannel AI Receptionists across all vertical markets is slated for the first half of 2026, enabling 24/7 automated patient interaction.

The second half of 2026 will focus on extending AI capabilities into autonomous intake and payments, including automated payment requests after claims adjudication.

Management expects gross revenue retention to trend back toward historical ranges of 91% to 93% as newer vertical cohorts mature and integration depth increases.

Operating income guidance of $8 million to $12 million for 2026 reflects a strategy to flow an increased percentage of incremental revenue into profitability while maintaining growth investments. Net revenue retention (NRR) of 93% in Q4 reflects the lapping of a 2024 price increase that previously provided a 250 basis point uplift.

Management highlighted a shift in the go-to-market model from a full-service Account Executive (AE) approach to a more efficient SDR/AE model to drive sales productivity.

02/18/2026 - 08:00 AM

Weave’s New Insurance Eligibility Solution Increases Dental Verification to 90% Average

LEHI, Utah --(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Weave (NYSE: WEAV), a leading all-in-one customer experience and payments software platform for small and medium-sized healthcare businesses, today announced Weave Insurance Eligibility (WIE). This advanced solution provides dental practices with some of the most accurate, comprehensive, and instantly accessible insurance data in the industry.

While traditional Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) clearinghouses provide a foundation of data, they often leave critical gaps. By integrating Robotic Process Automation (RPA) technology, Weave customers can automatically retrieve real-time data from insurance portals, eliminating a well-known pain point that currently consumes hours of front-office time.

“At Vero Dental, we invest in the latest clinical technology, and it is vital that our administrative experience matches the world-class care our patients expect from our doctors,” said Heather Buckson, Office Manager at Vero Dental. “Weave Insurance Eligibility has been transformative, reclaiming critical time for my team to focus on meaningful patient interactions while significantly increasing our reimbursement accuracy and office throughput.”

Driving Operational Efficiency and Practice Growth

The introduction of RPA-driven eligibility allows dental practices to move away from administrative bottlenecks and toward patient-centric care:

Optimized Reimbursements: By providing more complete eligibility data upfront, offices can ensure claims are clean upon submission. This leads to faster payments and a significant reduction in outstanding accounts receivable balances.

By providing more complete eligibility data upfront, offices can ensure claims are clean upon submission. This leads to faster payments and a significant reduction in outstanding accounts receivable balances. Reclaiming Administrative Hours: Weave Insurance Eligibility frees staff from tedious phone calls and portal hopping to manually verify insurance. This allows teams to focus on patient experience and high-value tasks without adding headcount.

Weave Insurance Eligibility frees staff from tedious phone calls and portal hopping to manually verify insurance. This allows teams to focus on patient experience and high-value tasks without adding headcount. Enhanced Patient Trust: Transparent financial conversations are the bedrock of patient loyalty. By providing accurate out-of-pocket estimates at the point of care, practices increase case acceptance and build long-term trust.

“Our mission is to automate tedious, but critical tasks so healthcare providers spend their time working directly with patients,” said Cam Holt, Head of Product at Weave. “Integrating payer portals directly into the Weave platform doesn’t just give offices more data; it gives them better data. Customers are achieving an average verification rate of 90% , it is a massive milestone that directly impacts the bottom line of every practice we serve.”

To learn more about Weave Insurance Eligibility, visit https://www.getweave.com/weave-insurance-eligibility/.

Weave is a leading AI-powered patient communications and engagement platform purpose-built for small and medium-sized healthcare practices. Operating at the center of patient interactions, Weave brings together AI agent and staff conversations across voice and text into unified, intelligent workflows that power the entire patient journey. Authorized integrations with practice management systems enable Weave to power critical practice operations, such as scheduling, verification of insurance eligibility, and collecting payments. By embedding AI directly into practice workflows, Weave reduces administrative burden and delivers real-time insights that help practices run smarter and grow with confidence. Serving nearly 40,000 customer locations, Weave was named a 2025 Best Software Awards winner for healthcare software products by G2. To learn more, visit investors.getweave.com.

funding_news.title: Weave Communications Q2 Earnings Call Highlights
funding_news.ai_summary: Weave Communications reported a 15.5% increase in Q2 revenue to $67.5 million and improved profitability, despite a temporary shortfall in bookings due to a sales organization transition. The company also raised its full-year revenue outlook to $273-$275 million and its operating income forecast to $12-$14 million. The transition to a new sales structure was completed in August, with continued efforts to enhance sales productivity and efficiency.
funding_news.author: Ethan Ryder
funding_news.full_text:
Weave Communications Q2 Earnings Call Highlights

Weave Communications (NYSE:WEAV) reported second-quarter revenue growth and improved profitability, while management said a transition in its sales organization created a temporary bookings shortfall that prompted a revision to its full-year revenue outlook. Total revenue rose 15.5% year over year to $67.5 million in the second quarter, CEO Brett White said. Payments revenue grew at roughly twice the pace of total revenue, while the company added a record number of new locations on both a gross and net basis. Dental, Weave’s largest vertical, added more locations on a gross and net basis than in any of the preceding eight quarters. Weave’s non-GAAP operating income reached $3.2 million, compared with breakeven in the prior-year quarter, and operating margin improved to 4.7%. CFO Jason Christiansen said the company converted 34% of its year-over-year revenue growth into incremental operating income during the period. Weave’s non-GAAP operating income reached $3.2 million, compared with breakeven in the prior-year quarter, and operating margin improved to 4.7%. CFO Jason Christiansen said the company converted 34% of its year-over-year revenue growth into incremental operating income during the period. Profitability Improves as Sales Efficiency Rises Gross profit increased 16% year over year to $49 million, producing a gross margin of 72.6%, up 30 basis points from a year earlier. Subscription and payment-processing gross margin was 77.9%. Christiansen said customer-support costs declined as a percentage of revenue, aided by technology and AI adoption, product enhancements and self-service capabilities. Those improvements were partially offset by higher messaging usage fees, adjustments to certain vendor invoices and elevated credit-card fees associated with a larger group of customers paying annually in advance. Sales and marketing expense totaled $25.8 million, or 38% of revenue, improving by 160 basis points from the prior year and 240 basis points sequentially. General and administrative expense was $10 million, or 15% of revenue, while research and development expense also totaled $10 million, or 15% of revenue. The company ended the quarter with $78.5 million in cash and short-term investments, up $5.8 million sequentially. Cash provided by operating activities was $10.2 million, and free cash flow was $8.7 million. Weave said it generated positive free cash flow during the first half of 2026. Go-to-Market Changes Affect Outlook Management said it has been reorganizing its go-to-market organization to improve sales productivity and profitability. The company verticalized its inbound sales force during the first half of the year, assigning specialized sellers to key markets including dental and specialty medical. It also shifted outbound prospecting responsibilities toward a sales development representative, or SDR, model, allowing account executives to focus on demonstrations and closing sales. White said the changes produced positive early results, including record location additions and improved sales-and-marketing efficiency. However, the move created an adjustment period from May through July as lead generation shifted to SDRs and account executives changed their responsibilities. “It took time to calibrate the lead distribution with the appropriate execution, resulting in bookings slightly below our expectation, despite very strong demand,” White said. Christiansen said the effects of those bookings shortfalls will be more visible in revenue during the second half of the year. Weave accelerated the transition and completed the move to the revised outbound-sales structure in the first week of August. White said the outbound team is smaller following the changes, though some former sellers moved into SDR roles. For the full year, Weave now expects revenue of $273 million to $275 million. At the same time, it raised its non-GAAP operating-income outlook to $12 million to $14 million, reflecting expected operating-efficiency gains. For the third quarter, the company forecast revenue of $68.6 million to $69.6 million and operating income of $3 million to $4 million. AI Products, Payments and Healthcare Integrations White described Weave as an AI-powered patient engagement and payments platform for healthcare practices. The company said its tools are designed to help practices manage appointment scheduling, reduce administrative work and limit revenue leakage through payment and revenue-cycle workflows. Weave added 70% more AI-powered features to its platform over the past year, according to White. Custom AI interactions totaled 70 million during the second quarter, up 165% from a year earlier. Call Intelligence interactions increased 143%, with customers analyzing more than 14.5 million calls and identifying 810,000 unscheduled opportunities for staff follow-up. The company’s AI Receptionist can answer inbound calls and text messages, respond to common patient questions, and book, confirm, cancel and reschedule appointments. Weave introduced early access to voice capabilities for the product in May. White said certain AI features are sold as additional modules or as part of higher-priced product bundles. He also said increased functionality can improve customer retention and create additional payment-processing opportunities as more workflows lead to collecting patient balances. Payments volume growth accelerated in the first half of 2026 compared with the first half of the prior year, White said, though he did not provide a dollar figure for the volume. Specialty Medical Expansion Weave also expanded its relationship with athenahealth during the quarter, releasing a deeper integration with the athenaOne platform and joining athenahealth’s Marketplace. Management said the marketplace makes Weave’s offerings available to more than 160,000 specialty medical providers. White said Weave’s athenahealth integration advanced from what the company classifies as level one to level four. Christiansen said level one largely involves syncing basic patient-contact information, while level four provides read-and-write capabilities across multiple electronic health record tables. Management said deeper integrations can support higher average selling prices, better retention and lower customer-acquisition costs over time. Weave said it is earlier in specialty medical than in dental, optometry and veterinary markets, and has historically had fewer integrations in the medical market. Despite the sales-transition disruption, White said management has not seen weakening demand. He pointed to interest from dental support organizations seeking to standardize workflows across multiple practices, as well as momentum from the company’s partnership with the American Dental Association, which he said had become Weave’s second-most productive affiliate program within several months. About Weave Communications (NYSE:WEAV) Weave Communications is a technology company that provides integrated communications and customer management solutions tailored for small- to medium-sized local businesses. Headquartered in Lehi, Utah, the company developed a cloud-based platform that unifies voice calling, business texting, appointment reminders and payment processing within a single interface. The platform’s core offerings include a unified business phone system, two-way texting, automated appointment and recall reminders, secure payment acceptance and a basic customer relationship management module.

funding_news.full_text:
LEHI, Utah, Oct. 24, 2019 /PRNewswire/ -- Weave, the leader in customer communication, today announced it has closed a $70 million series D funding round led by new Weave investor Tiger Global Management, with additional funding from current Weave investors including Catalyst, Bessemer, Crosslink, Pelion and LeadEdge.
Weave's mission is to bring local businesses and the people they serve closer together. With an estimated 29 million small and medium businesses (SMB) in the U.S. alone, Weave's unique set of consolidated business tools and impressive growth year over year, the company is disrupting and improving the way businesses work and communicate.
"I'm extremely grateful to the thousands of customers who have helped Weave grow to where we are today. Our aim with this funding round is to exceed our customers' expectations at every touchpoint, investing heavily in the products we create, the markets we serve and the overall customer experience we provide," said Brandon Rodman, CEO at Weave. "I am insanely proud of the spectacular team we've attracted here at Weave and the amazing products we deliver. We will continue to invest in our customers, our products and our people to build a solid, sustainable, and scalable business. We look forward to our next steps in this amazing journey."
With this round of funding, Weave plans to expand and enhance its current product offering, develop its international presence, grow its team, and continue to invest in the development of its employees.
"We've been investors in Weave since 2017. We particularly respect their extremely human leadership style," said Tyler Newton, partner at Catalyst Investors. "Weave is a place where employees are given challenging work and opportunities to grow, and they are also supported by a leadership team who invests in their long term development so they can deliver their best work. Not to mention, Weave has some of the best retention numbers we've ever seen for an SMB SaaS company. We're continually impressed by their accelerated growth and results. Catalyst is proud to be a partner with Weave."
Weave is one of the fastest-growing privately held companies in the U.S. The company doubled its revenue in 2018 and has increased its team at its Utah headquarters to approximately 550 employees, up from 300 at the beginning of the year. funding_news.full_text:
LEHI, Utah - Weave (NYSE:WEAV), a customer experience platform for healthcare businesses, announced today it has been selected as the exclusive patient engagement platform endorsed for American Dental Association members. The company, with a market capitalization of $374 million, has seen its stock decline 57% over the past year to $4.75, trading near its 52-week low. The endorsement follows a vetting process conducted by ADA Member Advantage to evaluate the effectiveness and value of Weave’s solutions, according to a press release statement. The designation is reserved for products and services that meet specific standards for dental practices. "We are excited to launch this new relationship with Weave," said Dr. Allen Reavis, chair of the ADA Member Advantage board of directors. "They have a deep understanding of dentistry and what happens in the front office of a dental practice." ADA members who sign up for Weave’s platform will receive discounts and enhanced training. The platform includes tools such as a phone system that displays patient information during calls, an AI-powered receptionist that follows up on missed calls, and insurance eligibility verification using robotic process automation. "We’re honored to support ADA members with technology solutions designed to deliver meaningful results," said David McNeil, Chief Revenue Officer at Weave. The endorsement comes as analysts show growing confidence in the company’s trajectory, with three analysts recently revising earnings upwards and predicting profitability this year, according to InvestingPro data. The platform provider generated $239 million in revenue over the last twelve months with 17% growth. The platform integrates with practice management systems to handle scheduling, insurance verification, and payment collection. Weave serves nearly 40,000 customer locations and was named a 2025 Best Software Awards winner for healthcare software products by G2. The ADA represents 159,000 dentist members across the United States. The association’s Member Advantage program evaluates products and services before granting endorsements to ensure they meet industry standards. In other recent news, Weave Communications reported mixed fourth-quarter results, with its adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint surpassing Wall Street expectations. Following these results, Stifel lowered its price target for Weave Communications to $9 from $11 but maintained a Buy rating. Piper Sandler also adjusted its outlook, reducing the price target to $8 from $12 while keeping an Overweight rating. This adjustment comes as Weave Communications experienced its second consecutive quarter of 17% year-over-year growth, primarily driven by a 35% increase in payments growth and record location additions in the specialty medical sector, alongside the acquisition of TrueLark. Meanwhile, EverCommerce has seen a change in analyst sentiment as Raymond James downgraded the company from Outperform to Market Perform. This decision was influenced by EverCommerce’s significant stock outperformance in recent months. Despite the downgrade, EverCommerce’s recent performance has been strong compared to sector benchmarks. AI Voice Call Credits introduced as a consumption-based pricing model layered on top of subscriptions (overage fees, monthly expiration) signals a new pricing model that aligns Weave's monetization with AI usage intensity, supporting upside as AI adoption scales.

WIE insurance eligibility (Feb 2026) and Call Intelligence (sentiment, revenue-opportunity detection) extend the product surface into RPA-driven revenue-cycle automation and analytics, deepening platform attachment beyond communications.

CareCredit (Synchrony) integration (Feb 2026) embeds patient financing into Weave Payments, with 43% of Weave payment customers indicating they would exclusively use Weave with the addition — a meaningful ecosystem buildout around the payments surface.

company_assessment.market_position: Weave Communications, Inc. (NYSE: WEAV) is a publicly-traded, healthcare-focused customer communications and payments SaaS company headquartered in Lehi, Utah. The company serves more than 40,000 customer locations across dental, specialty medical, optometry, veterinary, and medical-spa verticals, processing more than 1 billion patient interactions annually. It is the exclusive patient engagement platform endorsed by the American Dental Association for 159,000 dentist members, holds the #2 spot on G2's 2026 Best Healthcare Software list, and operates within an estimated $22 billion total addressable market following its 2025 acquisition of TrueLark. Q1 2026 revenue reached $65.5 million (17.4% YoY growth) and FY2026 guidance was raised to $275–$278 million.

strengths.details: Specialty medical is at ~1% penetration of a market that expanded by ~$7B to ~$22B following TrueLark. Going forward, AI Receptionist, omnichannel voice+text, and AI Receptionist early access for Dentrix/Eaglesoft/Open Dental users (25% off through 2026) should drive multi-year tailwinds in this underserved vertical. The 600+ location specialty medical win validates the enterprise play and creates a repeatable motion to scale ARPU meaningfully beyond the dental ceiling.
strengths.headline: Specialty medical expansion unlocks $22B TAM

strengths.details: AI product adoption surged >300% in platform-handled interactions in Q1 2026, and >50% of customer locations use at least one embedded AI feature. Consumption-based pricing on AI Voice Call Credits (usage with overages) layers on top of the subscription base. As AI Receptionist graduates from early-access discount to full pricing, we expect meaningful ARPU expansion and net revenue retention to accelerate above the current 17% organic growth.
strengths.headline: AI adoption compounds into ARPU expansion

strengths.details: Payments revenue is growing at >2x total company revenue rate (FY2025: total revenue +17%). CareCredit integration embedded in 2026 with 43% of payment customers indicating they would exclusively use Weave's services with financing—turning payments from a feature into a retention and monetization flywheel. As payment volume scales, this high-margin, transaction-based stream should disproportionately lift blended gross margin (already at 73.3% record).
strengths.headline: Payments flywheel drives margin-rich mix shift

strengths.details: ADA exclusive endorsement grants Weave privileged access to 159,000 dentist members with discounts and co-marketing. Combined with >40,000 customer locations, 1B+ annual patient interactions training proprietary LLMs, and integration depth across 40+ EHR/PMS systems, Weave is building the healthcare-specific data and distribution moat that general-purpose AI vendors cannot replicate. This verticalized training corpus should improve model accuracy, reduce hallucination risk in HIPAA-sensitive contexts, and compound as more practices adopt AI features.
strengths.headline: ADA endorsement + data moat deepens defensibility

strengths.details: FY2025 free cash flow turned positive at $12.9M, with management expecting positive FCF for H1 2026. Record 73.3% gross margin (Q4 2025) provides a path to GAAP profitability as growth investments moderate. Subscription-based revenue (~17% YoY, beating guide for 17 consecutive quarters) combined with payments expansion enables leverage as AI features compress service costs. The transition from cash-burn to cash-generation unlocks strategic optionality (M&A, buybacks) and reduces activist overhang over time.
strengths.headline: Positive FCF inflection enables reinvestment optionality

weakness.details: Engine Capital and 2717 Partners secured board seats via a cooperation agreement in March 2026, plus the formation of a dedicated Finance Committee. Activist pressure increases the risk of forced strategic changes, capital return demands, or management turnover that distracts from operational execution and could derail the multi-year AI build-out. The new directors (Dubin, Robson) did not come through normal succession, suggesting shareholder dissatisfaction with capital allocation or pace of profitable growth.
weakness.headline: Activist investor presence threatens strategic disruption

weakness.details: Weave reported -$18.9M EBITDA in FY2025, narrowing from -$39M in FY2021. As a public SaaS with growth decelerating to ~17% (vs. ~25% at IPO), the company remains structurally unprofitable on a GAAP basis and may face public-market valuation compression if growth continues to slow or if capital markets tighten. Negative operating income of -$28.9M suggests margin expansion could be more elusive than gross margin (73%) implies.
weakness.headline: Path to profitability remains unproven at scale

weakness.details: Weave prices subscription contracts with annual escalator clauses of up to 10% per 12-month period. In a competitive patient engagement market with point solutions (NexHealth, Solutionreach, Birdeye, etc.) and AI-native entrants, sustained 10% price hikes risk customer churn at SMB practices. Bundling raises unit economics but also raises the bar for switching costs—any lapse in service quality could push cost-sensitive dental and medical practices to disaggregated alternatives.
weakness.headline: Pricing power constrained by SMB churn sensitivity

weakness.details: TrueLark integration expanded TAM by ~$7B to $22B, but Weave acknowledges specialty medical is at ~1% market penetration. Low penetration can reflect both opportunity and structural friction—specialty medical workflows are more fragmented, have stricter HIPAA/clinical compliance needs, and depend on deep EHR integrations (athenahealth is 160,000 providers, but only a fraction are live). Closing the gap requires multi-year sales cycles and elevated S&M spend that could compress operating margins.
weakness.headline: Specialty medical penetration is a double-edged signal

weakness.details: Weave's competitive moat rests on EHR/PMS integrations (Dentrix, Eaglesoft, Open Dental, athenahealth, Planet DDS, etc.) and its AI models trained on 1B+ annual patient interactions. Hyperscalers (Microsoft, Google—its Gemini partner), Salesforce Health Cloud, and AI-native startups (e.g., Abridge, Suki) are pouring capital into healthcare AI. As cloud providers, EHR vendors, or new entrants build comparable conversational + voice AI, Weave's lead could erode as practices consolidate spend with strategic vendors.
weakness.headline: Big Tech and AI-native entrants threaten the moat

competitive_moat.details: Weave holds the exclusive patient engagement platform endorsement from the American Dental Association (ADA) for its 159,000 dentist members — a third-party validated, single-vendor designation that competitors cannot replicate without ADA approval. This endorsement is reinforced by G2 #2 Best Healthcare Software 2026 ranking and ADA Member Advantage vetting.

Weave processes over 1 billion patient interactions annually across 40,000+ customer locations, building a decade-plus proprietary healthcare conversation dataset used to train domain-specific LLMs. This corpus, combined with RPA-built payer-portal integrations yielding 90% insurance verification rates, is difficult for new entrants to replicate.

Weave is integrated with 40+ EHR/PMS systems including Dentrix, Eaglesoft, Open Dental, athenahealth, and Planet DDS, embedding itself into daily clinical workflows. The athenahealth Marketplace listing alone provides distribution access to 160,000+ providers, creating ecosystem-level lock-in beyond the individual customer relationship.

The unified all-in-one platform consolidates telephony, SMS, payments, scheduling, reviews, and AI receptionist into a single product with annual contracts, multi-location management, and aggregated reporting for DSOs. With more than 50% of customers using embedded AI features and payments revenue growing 2x the company average, switching costs compound as more workflows migrate onto Weave.

Multi-channel distribution combines direct field/inside sales, the athenahealth Marketplace (160,000+ providers), ADA Member Advantage channel, and the Minted Technology Advisors certified partner program. The 600+ location specialty medical group win demonstrates enterprise sales capability, while the website's PLG-style product tour supports SMB self-service conversion.

key_risks.details: Engine Capital and 2717 Partners entered a cooperation agreement in March 2026, securing two new board seats (Ryan Dubin, Edward Robson) and forming a dedicated Finance Committee chaired by David Silverman. Activist campaigns often pressure management teams to consider strategic reviews, capital returns, or leadership changes that can distract from operational momentum in a competitive AI build-out cycle.
key_risks.headline: Activist investor involvement elevates governance and execution risk

key_risks.details: FY2025 GAAP operating income was -$28.9M and net income was -$28.1M, although EBITDA improved to -$18.9M (from -$39.0M in 2021) and free cash flow turned positive at $12.9M. The gap between FCF inflection and GAAP profitability means heavy ongoing reinvestment in R&D (especially AI/Gemini build-out) and S&M, and any deceleration in revenue would compress margins quickly.
key_risks.headline: Sustained GAAP unprofitability despite improving cash profile

key_risks.details: Subscription fees can increase up to 10% in any 12-month period. Cost-sensitive SMB dental and medical practices have multiple alternatives (NexHealth, Solutionreach, Birdeye, Podium); aggressive annual escalators risk motivating switches, particularly for long-tenured customers with minimal ongoing feature uplift.
key_risks.headline: Subscription escalator clause could trigger SMB churn

key_risks.details: Dental remains the dominant vertical, with the ADA endorsement providing member access to 159,000 dentists. Any downturn in DSOs, dental practice openings, or insurance-driven elective procedure volume would disproportionately hit Weave versus more diversified healthcare platforms. Dental-vertical dependency also caps reimbursement-driven revenue ceiling relative to broader healthcare SaaS peers.
key_risks.headline: Heavy revenue concentration in dental vertical

key_risks.details: Weave operates only in the United States and Canada, with geographic restrictions explicitly noted. International expansion faces localization, regulatory, and EHR-integration barriers, while peer platforms with broader footprints are not similarly capped. Limited TAM expansion via geography means growth must come from share gains within North America.
key_risks.headline: Geographic concentration in U.S./Canada limits expansion optionality

key_risks.details: Weave's AI Receptionist is built on Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, and the company's value depends on continued partnership access and favorable pricing. Separately, EHR vendor partnerships (athenahealth, Dentrix, Eaglesoft, Open Dental, Planet DDS) could shift terms, bundle competing patient engagement features, or restrict API access—any of which would weaken Weave's integration moat and SMB go-to-market.
key_risks.headline: AI vendor and EHR platform risks on both sides

key_highlights.details: FY2025 revenue of $239.0M (+17.0% YoY); Q1 2026 revenue of $65.5M (+17.4% YoY) above guidance high end; FY2026 guidance raised to $275–$278M. Weave has met or exceeded revenue guidance for 17 consecutive quarters, reflecting strong forecast discipline and durable demand for its platform.
key_highlights.headline: Consistent 17% revenue growth with 17 straight guidance beats

key_highlights.details: Weave is the exclusive patient engagement platform endorsed by the American Dental Association for its 159,000 dentist members. Following a rigorous ADA Member Advantage vetting process, ADA members receive discounts and enhanced training—a powerful third-party validation and a meaningful distribution moat that competitors cannot replicate.
key_highlights.headline: Exclusive ADA endorsement unlocks 159,000 dentist member base

key_highlights.details: AI product adoption surged >300% in platform-handled interactions in Q1 2026, and over 50% of Weave customer locations now use at least one embedded AI feature. Combined with >1B annual patient interactions training proprietary LLMs and the Google Cloud Gemini-built AI Receptionist, this signals rapid conversion of the installed base to higher-ARPU AI-driven consumption.
key_highlights.headline: AI product adoption accelerating >300% in Q1 2026

key_highlights.details: Payments revenue is growing at more than 2x the total company revenue growth rate. With CareCredit integration (43% of payment customers would exclusively use Weave with financing) plus Text-to-Pay, BNPL, and payment plans, payments is becoming a margin-rich, transaction-based mix shift that expands ARPU and retention.
key_highlights.headline: Payments revenue growing >2x total company rate

key_highlights.details: Q4 2025 record gross margin of 73.3% (GAAP 72.7%), with full-year FY2025 free cash flow of positive $12.9M. Management expects free cash flow to remain positive in H1 2026, evidencing durable unit economics and a structural transition from cash-burn to cash-generation ahead of broader GAAP profitability.
key_highlights.headline: Record gross margins and positive FCF inflection

key_highlights.details: The 2025 TrueLark acquisition added omnichannel AI text-messaging patient engagement capabilities, expanding total addressable market from ~$15B to ~$22B. Specialty medical vertical is at ~1% market penetration, indicating significant upside runway now that AI omnichannel capabilities are integrated into the unified platform.
key_highlights.headline: TrueLark acquisition expanded TAM by ~$7B to ~$22B

key_highlights.details: Weave integrates with 40+ EHR/PMS systems including Dentrix, Eaglesoft, Open Dental, athenahealth (160,000+ providers), Planet DDS, and Practice Fusion. Plus the athenahealth Marketplace partnership and CareCredit embed deeply into daily practice workflows, raising switching costs and accelerating product-led discovery.
key_highlights.headline: 40+ EHR/PMS integrations create workflow embedding moat

customer_concentration.details: Weave serves over 40,000 customer locations across dental, medical, optometry, veterinary, and medical spa verticals, with the largest disclosed account being a 600+ location specialty medical group win — a meaningful but not dominant share of the installed base. Customer mix is heavily skewed to SMB dental practices (159,000 ADA-member dentist addressable base, ~1% specialty medical penetration), distributed across thousands of small-dollar subscription contracts. Annual contracts, 30-day SMB cancellation notice, and a consumption-based AI voice credit overlay create modest revenue predictability risk but very low single-customer concentration. Payments and AI usage-based revenue layers are growing 2x+ the company average, further diversifying the revenue base. The only concentration risk is vertical — dental remains the largest segment — but the athenahealth Marketplace integration and TrueLark-driven specialty medical push are actively de-concentrating that exposure.

peers.description: Solutionreach is one of Weave's closest direct competitors, providing patient communication, recall, reputation, and engagement software primarily to dental and medical practices. Both target SMB healthcare practices with all-in-one messaging, reminders, and front-office automation.
peers.name: Solutionreach

peers.description: NexHealth is a leading patient experience platform for dental and medical practices, offering online scheduling, patient messaging, digital intake, reviews, and EHR integrations. It competes directly with Weave in dental and is expanding into specialties, sharing Weave's API-first EHR integration thesis.
peers.name: NexHealth

peers.description: PatientPop, now part of Tebra, offers patient acquisition and communication tools (messaging, scheduling, reviews) for medical and dental practices. Direct overlap with Weave on patient communication, online scheduling, and reputation management for healthcare SMBs.
peers.name: PatientPop (by Tebra)

peers.description: Birdeye is a customer experience platform with reviews, messaging, and AI agents for multi-location SMBs. While broader than Weave (multi-vertical), Birdeye is increasingly competing in healthcare practices with comparable reputation management, two-way texting, and AI response offerings.
peers.name: Birdeye

peers.description: Demandforce (owned by Internet Brands) provides patient communication, appointment reminders, online reputation, and marketing automation for healthcare and wellness practices. It is a long-standing direct competitor in dental and medical SMB front-office communications.
peers.name: Demandforce

peers.description: Podium is a leading AI-powered customer interaction platform for SMBs including healthcare practices, providing messaging, reviews, payments, and AI webchat. It competes with Weave on AI-powered patient/lead communication and integrated payments for SMB verticals.
peers.name: Podium

peers.description: Klara is a healthcare-specific patient communication and collaboration platform focused on medical practices and health systems. It competes with Weave on omnichannel patient messaging, secure messaging, and EHR integration, with deeper clinical collaboration angle.
peers.name: Klara

peers.description: Luma Health provides patient engagement and scheduling automation for specialty medical practices, including self-scheduling, waitlist management, and AI-driven outreach. It overlaps with Weave's specialty medical expansion and appointment workflow focus.
peers.name: Luma Health

peers.description: TigerConnect is a broader healthcare communication platform focused on clinical team messaging, alarm management, and patient communication for hospitals and health systems. It is more enterprise/health-system-oriented than Weave but competes in healthcare messaging and engagement.
peers.name: TigerConnect

peers.description: RevenueWell, now part of DentalHQ, provides patient communication, recall, insurance verification, and marketing for dental practices. A direct competitor in dental front-office automation, mirroring Weave's dental-focused features including two-way texting and patient engagement.
peers.name: RevenueWell (by DentalHQ)
